# Decisions

Decisions made without Kev, newest at the bottom. Format and rules: Kev's global CLAUDE.md.

### DEC-2026-10-14-01: Generate waits for the balance; a failed balance read is no answer
Context: Kev: Generate flashed red with "Balance $0.00" while loading; he wants it disabled until the balance is known.
Options: (a) dim only while the first read is in flight; (b) also treat a failed read as "not loaded", press re-reads.
Decision: (b). A failed /api/billing/balance read no longer becomes a ready $0.00 (that was a second way to show a red
button). A press on the greyed button says "Your balance is still loading" and reads again, so a failed read never
leaves Generate stuck without a way out.
Evidence: VERIFIED 3465 tests passed; 7/7 in-memory mutants killed (__mutants-balance-gate.json). NOT verified in a
browser: the path needs a signed-in wallet. INFERRED: Kev's screenshot ("Loading images…" + red balance) cannot come
from enki main @a2cadcc4, where useImageViewModel.ts hides the red state while images load; likely an older deploy.
Revert: git revert of the commit that adds this entry.

### DEC-2026-10-14-03: the profile's Gallery tab as an endless wall with a side panel; /my-gallery removed
Context: Kev: no dates or numbers on the images; tight rows of one height, endless downwards; a click shows the
prompt data, Download and Share beside it. He meant Profile → Gallery (the private one). /my-gallery was an unlinked
duplicate page (nothing routed to it); Kev: "weg damit".
Options: (a) justified rows computed from known aspect ratios (the API returns no dimensions); (b) flex rows with a
fixed row height and each image at its natural width (no dimensions needed, the last row may stay short);
(c) a masonry of columns (rows not level).
Decision: (b) in components/gallery/GalleryWall: row height 220px (150px under 900px), 4px gaps, pages of 60 via the
API's offset, the next asked for when the end scrolls within 600px. The panel is a sticky 340px aside on wide screens
and a bottom sheet under 900px. Download uses the original file, the wall shows the preview. "Share + prompt" only
when the image is public and came from a prompt. Owner gets Publish and Remove (step-up 2FA as before); a visitor
gets Download and Share only. The tab's count badge stays.
Evidence: VERIFIED 3476 tests passed, 10/10 in-memory mutants killed (__mutants-profile-gallery.json), tsc (without
the dev server's stale route types) + eslint clean. NOT verified in a browser: the profile sits behind the beta gate.
Revert: git revert of the commit that adds this entry.

Update DEC-2026-10-14-03 (2026-10-15, Kev): rows are now JUSTIFIED: every row spans the full width, one height per
row, the height varies by row (target 280px, 180px under 900px; the last short row stays at the target). The API has
no image dimensions, so each image's ratio is read in the browser once it loads (1 until then). A click opens the
image near full screen (original file) with the details column beside it, arrows step through the wall, Escape or the
backdrop closes. Evidence: VERIFIED 3481 tests, 11/11 in-memory mutants killed (__mutants-justified.json).

### DEC-2026-10-15-01: gallery details, Recreate, marking and the are-you-sure, without new backend
Context: Kev (2026-10-15): the viewer must show the prompt text (and a bought prompt's values), Escape must close the
image only, Recreate must reopen the surface the image was made on, Quick Create idles as one corner button; later:
an "are you sure" before deleting, a checkbox + bottom bar for marked images, a heart that stays red.
Options: (a) wait for the backend pieces (decrypted text, a favorite flag) before any of it; (b) build every
frontend piece now against OPTIONAL fields (prompt_text, variable_values, prompt_kind, model_name, liked) and ask
Kev's go for the two backend pieces separately.
Decision: (b). Until the API returns them: the viewer says "No prompt recorded", the generator's name comes from the
catalogue client-side, Recreate treats every render with a prompt id as a listed prompt (image view), and the heart
is not rendered (the wall only shows it when liking is wired). Prompt text is encrypted at rest (generations.
final_prompt_ct etc.), so only the API can return it, and only to the owner; a bought prompt's text stays the
creator's, its values are the owner's. Deleting many runs the existing per-image DELETE (step-up 2FA stays).
Evidence: VERIFIED 3500 tests passed; mutants killed 11/11 (justified), 14/14 (recreate), 10/10 (select); tsc +
eslint clean; build green. NOT verified in a browser: the profile sits behind the beta gate.
Revert: git revert of the commits that add this entry's work (gallery: prompt details…, gallery: marking…).

### DEC-2026-10-15-02: the owner's view of a render: text and values opened server-side, owner only
Context: Kev (2026-10-15): "the prompt text and the variables must be visible when I open an image at gallery … the

unlisted prompt (Quick Create / editor), else "market". The route reads the envelope columns only for the owner.
Evidence: VERIFIED 3507 tests, 9/9 in-memory mutants killed; live read-only check against the production database
(service key, lengths only printed): 5 latest generations opened with the configured field key (kid field-v1),
kinds resolved. Build green.
Revert: git revert of the commit that adds this entry.

### DEC-2026-10-15-03: likes scale as one row each plus a counter on the target; images reuse the live table
Context: Kev (2026-10-15): a heart on gallery images; "every user collects unlimited likes, every image too". Likes
already live in public.reactions (one row each); the feed counted rows per page, the prompt route per request.
Options: (a) an array of liked ids on the user row (lost writes, no counts, no uniqueness); (b) a new image-likes
table; (c) the existing reactions table, indexed, with a like_count on the target kept by a trigger.
Decision: (c). Probed live 2026-10-15 with inserts that must fail on the FK: the CHECK already accepts target_type
'generated_image' and reaction_type 'like', so no constraint change. SQL 29 adds a unique index per (user, target,
reaction) and an index per target, like_count on prompts and generated_images (trigger in the same transaction,
never below 0, backfill), revokes the function from anon/authenticated. lib/likes.ts holds the logic for both
routes; the image route lets a viewer like only an image they may see (own; or public, checked, owner not hidden,
18+ only with the opt-in) and answers 404 otherwise. The feed reads like_count. Any signed-in viewer gets the heart
in a profile gallery; the bar's heart likes every marked image (image route limit 120/min).
Evidence: VERIFIED live CHECK/FK probe (23503 for prompt+generated_image, 23514 for image); PGlite 8 checks, 14/14
SQL mutants killed; 15 route/lib tests, 23/23 in-memory mutants killed; suite 3529; build green.
Order: SQL 29 must run BEFORE this code is deployed or pulled against the live DB (the feed and the like routes
select like_count).
Revert: git revert of the like commits; SQL rollback at the end of migrations/2026-10-15-like-counters.sql.

### DEC-2026-10-16-01: an external wallet connects silently first and gets 60 seconds to answer
Context: on Colosseum Solflare never opened its window; the payment waited forever and every queued payment behind
it (serial signer). Solflare also asked again on every payment although Kev ticked "Trust this website".
Options: deadline only; silent connect only; both; turn the provider's autoConnect back on (rejected: its comment
says a double connect after select() makes Solflare reject).
Decision: both, inside signForBuyer. adapter.autoConnect() (the Wallet Standard silent connect, no window) runs
first and its refusal is swallowed; the prompting connect() runs only when that did not connect. Connect plus
signature together get 60 s (same as requestCdpSign); after that the job fails with "Your wallet didn't answer.
Open it and try again — nothing was charged." The embedded (email) wallet path is unchanged: it already has its
own 60 s deadline, and its unlock dialog stays outside any deadline on purpose (lib/cdp-bridge.ts).
Evidence: VERIFIED node_modules/@solana/wallet-standard-wallet-adapter-base/lib/esm/adapter.js:105-110 (autoConnect
= connect({silent:true}), connect = prompting). INFERRED that Solflare's trust applies only to a silent connect; not
determined in a real browser (the built-in browser has no wallet extension). VERIFIED tests: payment-signer 15/15,
11/11 in-memory mutants killed; suite 3542 passed, 3 timeouts in other files that pass alone (29/29); tsc clean.
Residual: a wallet whose silent connect hangs holds connect() off (adapter "connecting" guard) until the 60 s end.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-02: Android: one helper for every external-wallet surface; the phone adapter is waited for, signs a VersionedTransaction, and takes two taps
Context: on Android Chrome the only external wallet is the Mobile Wallet Adapter (MWA, wallet-adapter-mobile 2.2.8, the
bridge to the wallet apps on the phone). Nothing worked with it, on prod and on the branch: the picker read the key before
the app had opened ("Wallet did not return a public key"), the second tap failed on MWA's cached signIn and wiped the
cache, payments refused every deposit (connect() returns before connecting; a partially signed legacy Transaction throws
in MWA's serialize before the app is asked), Send USDC never connected the wallet after a reload, linking failed on the
first tap. Kev: "ja prüf das mit android" / "ok fix das dann für android".
Options: (a) wait for the adapter's 'connect' event in each surface; (b) one helper used by all four surfaces; (c) upgrade
the library (upstream main 3.0.0 still drops the promise, PR #1660 open); (d) a one-trip signIn login (needs the nonce
unbound from the address: backend).
Decision: (b). lib/ui/kit/external-wallet.ts: connectAdapter (silent or prompting; waits while the phone adapter is still at
it; throws the wallet's refusal from the 'error' event; 60 s bound; connected AND key, since MWA keeps a stale key after
the wallet let go), signWithAdapter (VersionedTransaction in, the same bytes; serializes whatever comes back), the name and
label ("Use Installed Wallet", Solana Mobile's guideline) and the dialog helpers. Chrome launches an app once per tap, so a
prompting connect on the phone ends the tap: the picker shows "Connected - tap to sign in", LinkWalletButtons "Sign to
link", the payment signer and Send USDC say "connected, tap again". The picker never uses signIn on the phone (MWA answers
from its cache without a signature). MWA's own dialogs are hosts under body: a CSS rule keeps them tappable under Radix's
pointer lock, onInteractOutside keeps a tap in them from closing the picker. The guardian page (two taps already, reads
provider state) is unchanged.
Evidence: VERIFIED library: wallet-adapter-mobile index.browser.js:89-94 (connect drops its promise), :246
(value.serialize()); wallet-standard-mobile :1135-1138 (cache short-cut), :1340-1347 (signIn from the cache). VERIFIED
docs read this session: Solana Mobile ux-guidelines ("Use Installed Wallet"; signIn for one action); Chromium
external_intents README ("repeatedly attempting to launch apps with the same user activation" is blocked; 15 s; an XHR
then a redirect is allowed). VERIFIED tests over the REAL MWA adapter class with a fake wallet app (lib/__tests__/_mwa.ts):
external-wallet 19, payment-signer 18, link-wallet-client 10 = 47 passed; 24/24 in-memory mutants killed; suite 3566
passed with 2 timeouts in one-time-password.test.ts (pass alone); tsc clean; eslint clean. VERIFIED in the built-in browser
(Android UA, localhost:3009, the real library): the row reads "Use Installed Wallet"; a tap runs MWA, Chromium reports the
loopback permission denied, MWA's blocked dialog opens over the picker, its "Got it" closes it (listener fired, root
display none) and the picker stays open with "Couldn't connect (Use Installed Wallet): Local Network Access permission
denied." Not determined: a real Android phone with a wallet app (none here); the review's device-level claims are INFERRED.
Residual: one launch per tap means queued payments (several images) sign one per tap on the phone; a stale MWA cache after
log off (EnkiHome disconnects only a connected adapter); MWA authorizes on devnet (the app's RPC). Kev's device test needs
https (MWA is Unsupported on plain http: isSecureContext) or adb reverse.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-03: shown images are the WebP renditions, looked up by the original's URL; downloads stay the original
Context: Kev, 2026-10-16: every shown image a WebP without quality loss, Download on the image, the home page loads too
long, the image UI's examples open as PNG. Measured live: the feed's six cards were six PNG originals (1.8-5.9 MB,
16.3 MB a page, cards ~300 px wide). The WebP pipeline runs (39/40 new rows have preview 1280/q80 ~220 KB and thumb
384 ~25 KB), but prompts.showcase_images keeps the ORIGINAL URLs and the renditions live on generated_images under
names of their own (derivative-store: generations/<userId>/<ts>_<rand>.preview.webp), so no surface could derive one.
Options: (a) derive the rendition URL by name on the client (0/12 found: the names differ); (b) store renditions in
showcase_images (jsonb shape change, several readers); (c) look them up by storage_url when the page is built; (d) a
progressive viewer that swaps the PNG back in (defeats "WebP shown", re-downloads MBs).
Decision: (c), with Kev's go for the backend part. lib/marketplace/renditions.ts: renditionsByUrl (generated_images,
in storage_url, 40 URLs per query via inChunks' new size parameter; a failed read leaves the originals) and
withRenditions. enrichPromptCards (feed + search) and /api/prompts/[id] attach {url, preview, thumb} to every showcase
image. FeedCard loads thumb/preview by srcset+sizes (2/3/4 columns), the original only when a rendition fails; the
Image View's examples show the preview and download the original; the profile wall's tiles take the thumb, its viewer
the preview; the adapter reads preview first. The viewer shows the WebP only: no PNG swap.
Evidence: VERIFIED live probes (scratchpad, service key read into the header): 6/6 showcase URLs join to rows with
preview+thumb; after the change the running dev server (through the beta gate) answers /api/prompts/[id] with
.preview.webp/.thumb.webp and /api/marketplace/prompts?limit=6 with 6/6 thumbs. Tests: showcase-renditions 8 (fake
postgrest + source pins), card.test + wall pins updated; affected files 313 passed; 17/18 in-memory mutants killed,
the survivor was a dead guard (inChunks already answers an empty list) and is removed; suite 3578 passed, 320 files;
tsc clean; eslint only the pre-existing <img> warnings. Not determined: the rendered /home (behind the gate; Kev sees
it signed in).
Residual: previews are 1280/q80, soft in fullscreen on large screens: a 2048/q90 rendition for new images plus a
backfill is the open backend item; a fresh render in the editor still shows its original (the generate route answers
previewUrl: null); bookmark-folder icons keep the original URL.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-04: the Image View adds one history entry when opened over an address that names no prompt
Context: Kev: Back from the image UI landed on the landing page. The view wrote ?prompt=<id> with replaceState (no
entry), so the browser's Back left /home for the entry before it: the landing (login arrives by a full navigation).
Options: (a) pushState on open and history.back() on close (not StrictMode-safe: the dev double-mount pops the entry);
(b) pushState on open, replaceState without the prompt on close, and the feed closes the view when the address loses
its prompt; (c) leave it.
Decision: (b). EnkiDetailPanel: an address naming no prompt gets one entry per view instance (an `owned` ref); any other
address is changed in place (a reload, a link, a switch inside the view); closing takes the prompt out in place.
EnkiFeedPage: a searchParams change without a prompt closes the open view (the browser's Back). Cost: after a close
from inside, one Back is a no-op (the entry stays, without the prompt).
Evidence: VERIFIED code: the old replaceState at EnkiDetailPanel:55, ImageView's leave = onClose. Tests: open-link 8,
mounts 7 (useRef added to its React stand-in); 4/4 in-memory mutants killed; suite 3581 passed, 320 files; tsc clean.
Not determined in a browser (the pane sits behind the beta gate): Kev's check is card -> browser Back -> the feed, at
its scroll position.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-05: downloads are named enki-<title>-<file id>.<ext>
Context: Kev: names after the prompt title collide when several images share a title; he wants
"enki-[file-name]-[unique-identifier]" so that saving never collides.
Options: (a) a counter (today's title-n: collides across prompts and sessions); (b) the image row's uuid (plumbing into
every call site; a creator example has none); (c) the stored file's own blob name, read from its URL (unique per file by
construction: derivative-store names <ts>_<rand>), else a time+random stamp.
Decision: (c). lib/ui/kit/format.ts: downloadName(title, id, mime) and fileId(url); share.ts derives the id from the
URL, so every call site passes the title alone (the gallery its prompt's title, else none: enki-<id>). Share-sheet
files take the same name. ViewerPanel loses its unused `n`.
Evidence: VERIFIED format.test (names, fileId incl. rendition suffix, query, data: URL stamp), share.test, wall pins;
7/7 in-memory mutants killed; suite 3581 passed; tsc clean.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-06: the preview rendition is 2048 px at quality 90 for new images
Context: Kev wants every shown image as WebP without quality loss; 1280/q80 is soft in fullscreen on large screens.
Options: 1280/q80 (170-260 KB); 2048/q85 (540-710 KB); 2048/q90 (810-930 KB); lossless WebP (~2/3 of the PNG, no point).
Decision: 2048/q90. Measured (scratchpad bench, sharp effort 2) on our own 2K originals: JPEG 2.9 MB -> 842 KB, PNG
7.1 MB -> 926 KB, encoded in 220-420 ms (was 110-220 ms), inside the store deadline. Thumbs carry the grids, so the
feed's weight is unchanged. Applies to NEW images; the 50 existing rows keep 1280/q80 until a backfill (Blob writes and
DB updates), which waits for Kev's go. FeedCard's srcset keeps the 1280w descriptor: with two candidates the browser's
choice is the same either way.
Evidence: VERIFIED bench numbers above; image-derivatives.test pins the long edge at exactly 2048 (the 1280 mutant is
killed); suite 3581 passed; tsc clean.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-11: a database outage is two health runs in a row without an answer, each after three tries
Context: Kev got "Enki: database unreachable" at 08:00 and "database back" at 08:05, twice ("we gotta fix that shit"). The
cron asked once with a 10 s timeout and alerted on the first failure; it dropped the error, so the cause cannot be read
back. Supabase's status history shows no database, API or pooler incident from 10-01 to 10-16; no writes landed in the
window either way (06:00 UTC is quiet), so "was it really down" is not determined.
Options: retry inside a run; require two failed runs in a row; both; a longer timeout alone.
Decision: both. Up to 3 tries 5 s apart (maxDuration 60), then a suspect marker in Blob; the next run (5 min later)
alerts if it fails too and clears the marker silently if it answers. The mail names when it started and the last
error, and the run logs it, so the next incident has a cause. A real outage alerts 5 minutes later than before.
Evidence: VERIFIED old route answered `!error` of one select; tests db-health-cron 10 (the October case, retry within a
run, the 5 s pause, two-run alert with the error, retries of unsent mails); 10/10 in-memory mutants killed; outage
neighbours (db-outage-503, db-outage-paths, cron-sweep) green; tsc clean.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

### DEC-2026-10-16-13: reads retry twice on a transient failure; writes never retry on their own
Context: Kev: "was passiert denn mit unseren angezeigten daten?". The QueryClient had retry: false and staleTime
Infinity: shown data stays, but anything loaded during a blip failed at once ("Couldn't load the feed").
Options: retry every failed query (a 404 or a bug would wait 4 s for nothing); retry only transient failures; leave it.
Decision: queries retry twice, after 1 s and 3 s, only on a 502/503/504, the database's 503 sentence, or a request the
network dropped (lib/queryClient.ts isTransientFailure). Mutations keep retry: false: nothing that pays or writes is
sent twice by itself. Every query that throws is a read; the two quote queries POST but return null on failure, so they

### DEC-2026-10-17-03: the render switch asks at a render's first request, once per confirmation for every render
Context: the "render" row of the Settings table (DEC-2026-10-17-02) needed a gate. A paid render runs: wallet unlock
(embedded wallets) -> intent -> authorize (build) -> sign -> submit (money moves) -> one generate-image per unit; a free
render is one POST /api/generate-free. The editor, image view, render queue and Quick Create all end in
runGenerationBatch; queue jobs run in parallel, and a second step-up ask closes an open one.

escrow), or the intent; ask per render or hold one confirmation; ask proactively from the client or let the server ask.
Decision: the server asks at POST /api/payments/generation/intent (before anything is priced, built or signed; keyed
on the stable users.id via resolveStableUserId, since requireAuth gives the session's wallet) and at the top of
POST /api/generate-free (before the prompt check and the daily claim). The client (lib/ui/kit/render-stepup.ts) lets
the server decide, asks once on its 401, holds the token for 4 of its 5 minutes, sends it with every following
render, shares one dialog between parallel jobs, and asks anew when a held token is refused. A cancel reads "Not
confirmed. Nothing was charged." (paid) or "Not confirmed. Nothing was generated." (free). Resume and retry never open
an intent, so they are not asked. Stated residual: an embedded-wallet user with rendering on and a locked wallet sees
the wallet dialog and then the render dialog; a render confirmation does not unlock the wallet.

on the next render, one dialog for three parallel renders, a refused token asks anew, cancel detected) and

route answers "This setting is not available yet" (PGRST202 or 42703).

open an intent" holds for resuming a pending deposit, not for retrying a job refused at its intent.

scope already open or waiting shares that dialog, a cancel or a failing dialog lets the next one open. Correction:

intent and is asked again unless a held render confirmation is still fresh.

after a cancel and after a failing dialog the next opens; the provider asks through it); 5 of 5 in-memory mutants

### DEC-2026-10-17-12: a Google or X account gets its wallet without a password row
Context: the wallet JWT route opened the wallet only for a confirmed password email, and the wallet runtime mounted

could sign in but never hold or spend money.

signs in; a second factor still locks it the same way); a password account is still judged by its password row,
identity or not. The JWT carries email only when there is one (CDP requires iss, sub, exp, iat; email is optional).
The runtime is keyed by account: the email, or the session for an account without one; nothing is remembered for
an account without email (the remembered address was keyed by email, and a session token is not written anywhere).
Evidence: REPORTED (docs.cdp.coinbase.com/embedded-wallets/custom-authentication, fetched 2026-10-17): "checks
required claims (iss, exp, iat, and your configured user identifier claim)", email only as an optional identifier.

another user's identity or a failed read keeps it closed, 400 and 503; a password account with an identity is still
asked to confirm its email), cdp-wallet-bridge 23 (runtime key pin), env-01 12 passed; 6 of 6 in-memory mutants
killed (identity check, identity read error, identity of another user, social refused, password check skipped,
empty email claim) plus the runtime key; tsc exit 0, eslint 0 errors.

### DEC-2026-10-17-65: licence_credits, the licence fees Enki owes for x402 renders
Context: Kev, 2026-10-17: "verkäufer-modell für künstlerprompts" on x402: Enki sells the render, the buyer pays Enki

### DEC-2026-10-17-66: x402 is a merchant: the buyer pays Enki the whole price, Enki owes the licence
Context: Kev, 2026-10-17: "verkäufer-modell für künstlerprompts" for x402. Until now an artist or referred prompt
settled as a source split: the 402 listed one TransferChecked per share (artist, Enki, referrer, author) and the
buyer's own transaction paid each one. This REVERSES, for x402 only, the recorded rule of 2026-07-05 ("Artist
payouts: split at source ... Enki NEVER holds artist money", memory payment-design-decisions.md:13) and the route's
own header (route.ts:23-24 before this commit, "the same atomic source-split the human rails settle with. The artist
is paid by the buyer's own transaction"). The escrow and web rails keep the source split.
Options: keep the split (PayBox and other standard clients build one transfer to payTo, so a multi-leg 402 fails for
them); merchant model with the shares owed and recorded (licence_credits, DEC-65).

A unit whose recorded signature differs from the rebuilt one means its nonce moved, which only the handed-out payment's broadcast does (Enki is the nonce authority and advances nothing else): the order is voided ("rejected", so settleVoided looks up S1 and books a refund if it landed without an image) and the buyer hears "This order's payment was already sent from your wallet. ### DEC-2026-10-19-121: a landed capture always ends with its booking known and a refund owed always has its row (round 3: V2; completes DEC-111)
Context: round 3 found DEC-111's inline refund-owed write could leave a paid, withheld image with no refund row and nothing that revisits it: bookPaidUndelivered treated an error like "no row" and ignored a failed insert of the refund row, and bookedOnce re-read only fulfilled_at, so a row booked refund-owed by a lost answer read as not delivered while the sweep (which selects captured_at IS NULL) never saw it again.

### DEC-2026-10-19-128: a void's nonce is recorded closed only once its payment is settled (round 4: C1, C11)

### DEC-2026-10-19-267: the node's signature-verification refusal is the payer's, not an outage (round 30: C1, high, latent since DEC-122)

### DEC-2026-10-21-325: only the route's own "Not signed in" ends a session in the browser
Context: correction to DEC-2026-10-21-318, from an adversarially verified review. BetaGate forgot the session on ANY 401 from /api/users/handle. During the whitelist stage (TEAM_ACCESS_CODE set) the proxy answers every closed API without the team cookie with its own 401 {"error":"Access code required"} (proxy.ts), and a banned account never holds that cookie (password-login.ts, the OAuth callback and /api/ban/me revoke it). So on /banned the check deleted a banned user's email/Google/X session, and the appeal and the USDC withdrawal (session-bound) stopped working. The method misled because DEC-318 read the route's code, not the proxy in front of it.
Options: skip the forget on /banned; forget only on the route's own answer.
Decision: the second. BetaGate forgets only when the 401's body says "Not signed in" (the route's words, app/api/users/handle GET); the proxy's 401 keeps the session. Residual risk, left for Kev because the fix is security territory (lib/session-user.ts): only network failures count as "database unreachable" there, so a Supabase 5xx or statement timeout reads as "no session" and the route answers "Not signed in"; since DEC-318 that logs the browser out (in every tab) during such an incident. The two-line fix is to throw DbUnreachableError on any lookup error, so the route answers 500 and the session stays.
Evidence: VERIFIED: tsc exit 0; eslint 0; beta-gate-recheck, adult-confirm, beta-gate-whitelist-admit and store-session "41 passed"; 3/3 in-memory mutants killed (scratchpad ui-v2/mutants/login2.json): forgetting on any 401 turns 2 tests red, matching the proxy's words or a route that says something else turns 1 red. REPORTED (review subagents): the banned chain end to end, and that TEAM_ACCESS_CODE is set in .env.local. Blind spot: no rendered BetaGate; the review's DB-error path was read from code, not provoked.
Revert: git revert of this commit (DEC-318's behaviour returns).

### DEC-2026-10-21-327: a failed session or ban lookup is an outage, never "not signed in" or "not banned"
Context: Kev's go (2026-10-21, "ja fix") on DEC-2026-10-21-325's residual risk. lib/session-user.ts threw DbUnreachableError only for a dead host (cf492c4e, 2026-09-05); any other lookup error (a Supabase 5xx, PGRST000 "cannot connect", a statement timeout, a refused permission) read as "no session", and the handle route answered "Not signed in", which since DEC-318 makes the browser forget the session in every tab. The same rule made a failed ban read count as "not banned" (fail-open).
Options: keep network-only; enumerate the transient codes; treat every lookup error as unreadable.
Decision: every lookup error throws DbUnreachableError (routes answer 503 as for a dead host), in resolveSessionUserWithBan, activeBanFor and resolveOwnerIds; only PGRST116 ("several rows" from maybeSingle) still reads as no single match, as before. This deliberately reverses the 09-05 test "an ordinary query error is not mistaken for an outage": a refused permission now answers 503 instead of 401/404 (fail-closed either way, and the session survives). Two tests elsewhere that pinned the old rule (owner-ids-outage, live-prompt-quote) now expect the outage. Security territory: committed on the UI branch for Kev's testing and on its own branch sec/session-lifetime (from enki/main) for its own PR.
Evidence: VERIFIED: tsc exit 0; eslint 0; session-user, owner-ids-outage and live-prompt-quote tests "32 passed"; 5/5 in-memory mutants killed (scratchpad ui-v2/mutants/sec1.json). Collision check: no open PR on EnkiArtAI/enki (gh pr list: []), no foreign commit since 10-14 on these files after `git fetch enki`. Blind spot: route-level 503 handling read from tests, not provoked against Supabase.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

Two defects found on the way and fixed: the size never reached the editor (.iv-pm sets its own --kit-fs, so the wrapper passes --iv-fs), and the editor re-measures only when its min changes, so min is one exact line (size * 1.7 + 14; the rounded form gave 23 and 23.5 px the same min). fitFont searches whole half pixels (the float bisection returned 24.5 where 25 fit).
Evidence: VERIFIED in the bench page (real CSS, system-ui font, emulated autosize): Kev's chiaroscuro prompt at 2048x1103 fits at 27 px, field = probe = 473 px, 46 px to the agent row (less than one more 46 px line), agent row 10 px over the scroller's foot, focus changes the field's height by 0; twice that prompt stays at 19 px; at 1440x900 a one-line prompt fits at 35 px, 18 px from the agent row. Tests: image-view + kit "699 passed"; 26/26 in-memory mutants killed (scratchpad ui-v2/mutants/plain-fit.json). Blind spots: not measured in the gated app with Geist; a one-line prompt on a tall screen still leaves room at 36 px (2048x1103: 383 px).

### DEC-2026-10-26-373: the trial batch's review fixes, and a correction to DEC-366
Context: an adversarial review of f98047c7..99439f45 (wf_093bee73-fbb: 3 lenses, each finding checked by a skeptic) confirmed 17 findings; all are fixed here except one (below).
CORRECTION to DEC-366: it said a Google or X login off the access list "still gets a session". Wrong: lib/auth/oauth.ts resolveIdentity throws not_whitelisted for such a login (line 497-498 then) before the callback mints anything; the callback's "if (!allowlisted) return res" that misled me cannot be reached by a login. The /api/ban/me hole was therefore narrow: sessions of accounts that no longer pass the list (taken off it, or listed while still 'user'). The fix stays right; its urgency was overstated, and its role test was wrong in both directions (a removed member stays 'beta'; a listed account may still be 'user').
Decision (the fixes):
1. Google/X trials could never start (high): resolveIdentity takes trialPass (this browser holds a pass) and admits an off-list login with a pass or a running trial; the callback spends the code, and with no trial after all it mints no session and removes an account made for the login.
2. trialAdmission reads the pass first: a second code is spent even while an earlier trial runs; the trial that ends last counts.
3. Password login: a suspended account spends no code (refused as any off-list login); when the password was right and the browser holds a pass but no trial comes of it, it answers 403 "Your trial with this code has ended, or the code can no longer be used." instead of "Wrong login or password". The reset-code login takes a trial the same way (session to the trial's end, its cookie, no beta).
4. /api/ban/me gives the team cookie when the access list admits the account (accountAllowed, as every login asks) or it is staff; a tester's running trial gets the trial cookie.
5. A ban (revokeGateCookie) takes the trial cookie too.
6. Revoke signs testers out by user id and by their wallet addresses (a session is keyed by the wallet once one is attached), as a password reset does.
7. The shell moves under the trial line (ek-with-banner), which covered its top 30 px.
8. The Trials form refuses an empty custom budget (it made a $0 code).
Not fixed: the email sign-in from /gate lands on /home rather than ?next= (low); the admin sidebar is 208 px at 375 px (older than this batch, a page-shell change); a revoke that fails half-way cannot be retried from the panel (the trial is inactive already).
Evidence: VERIFIED: whole suite "4836 passed" before the pins below; 11 in-memory mutants, 9 killed at once; the 2 survivors were source pins read by relative path, which the mutant runner does not reach (__bench-mutant.setup.mjs matches absolute paths): trial-logins and mobile-menu now read by absolute path, and those mutants (plus the phone menu's) are killed, 0 survivors.
Revert: git revert of this commit.

Context: Kev (2026-10-27): "i also dont wanna see the top menü when scrolling through ANY menü, this goes also for profile". ### DEC-2026-10-27-434: signed out, the server walls the app too: a signed member cookie, the landing as the way in
Context: Kev (2026-10-27): "ja go, wieso aufm server aussperren?" on my offer to lock signed-out visitors out on the server as well as in the browser (DEC-418 did the browser). The proxy opened every page and API for the cookie enki_team holding the team code itself: anyone who knew the code could set it, a logout left it for up to 30 days (wallet sessions end after 24 h), and the public read APIs (feed, prompts, profiles) answered such a browser without a session. The session itself is a header token in localStorage, so the proxy cannot see it.
Options: (a) the cookie becomes a signed "member" cookie (lib/trial-cookie's HMAC, kind-separated, AUTH_PEPPER), set by every login of an admitted account until that session's end, taken by a logout and by any route that finds no session; (b) a session lookup in the proxy on every request (a database read per page and API call); (c) keep the code cookie and only revoke it on logout (still forgeable by everyone who knows the code).
Decision: (a). grantGateCookie(res, subject, sessionExpiresAt) signs kind "member" for the account (wallet login: user id, else the address) with Expires = the session's end; the six login paths pass their session (oauth callback, register, reset-code, password login, wallet session, /api/ban/me). The proxy opens the app for a valid member or trial cookie only; the team code opens nothing; a walled page goes to "/" (the landing) with nothing appended (Kev: "immer zu home pls nach landing page"), a walled API keeps its 401 "Access code required". DELETE /api/auth/session (logout, email and wallet), GET /api/users/handle and GET /api/ban/me revoke the cookie when there is no live session. /api/gate: the team code sets no cookie and the page goes on to the landing's sign-in (/?login=1); GET reports team for a valid member or trial cookie. The landing renews a signed-in browser's missing cookie through /api/ban/me (which now says admitted: true) and then opens /home, once a minute at most.
Consequence: on the first visit after a deploy every signed-in browser still holds the old code cookie; the proxy sends it to the landing, which renews it from the session and opens /home (one extra hop, no new login).
Evidence: VERIFIED member-cookie.test.ts (13: signed cookie, Expires = session end, no cookie off-stage/without pepper/without an end, the proxy walls the bare code, ended, forged, pass and trial-kind values and a member value under the trial's name, landing redirect without a query, API 401, logout with and without a token, identity and ban/me revoke, ban/me renews only a listed account, /api/gate sets nothing, the landing's renewal), gate-whitelist-status.test.ts rewritten (6 cookie cases), 9 test files' pins moved (banned-door, oauth-routes, trial-logins, trial, session-lifetime, allowlisted-is-beta, beta-gate-recheck, gate-next); 21 in-memory mutants, 20 killed, 1 equivalent (OAuth cookie end = now + 30 d equals the 30-day session) killed when made distinguishable (31 d): "survivors: 0 of 1".
Live on the dev server (VERIFIED, scratchpad __gate-live.mjs, the code never printed): no cookie and the bare team code: /home and /generator/x?tab=2 -> "307 /", /api/prompts -> "401"; POST /api/gate with the team code -> 200 {"ok":true,"signIn":true}, 0 Set-Cookie; GET /api/gate with the bare code -> team false. The pane (signed in, old cookie) opened "/" and went on by itself: GET /api/ban/me 200, then /home with every API 200 and /api/gate team true. tsc exit 0; whole suite "404 passed / 4951 passed" (--maxWorkers=4).
Revert: git revert of this commit; signed-in browsers then need the team code cookie again (a fresh login sets it).

### DEC-2026-10-28-482: MoreBelow counts the rows inside a display: contents wrapper, and re-measures as the composer's rows change

### DEC-2026-10-29-515: Enki-wide figures counted in one database function; what counts as artist revenue
Context: Kev 2026-10-29: "wir brauchen auch bei den analytics auch Enki-global analytics, wie users, posted images, generated images, generated revenue for artists, views, halt genauso wie hier: https://hup.social/leaderboard". Enki had no platform figures. The two "earnings" displays (/api/analytics/me, the Hall of Fame) read prompt_purchases, which nothing writes (VERIFIED: grep finds readers only, 0 rows live); artist money is recorded per render in micro-USDC on three rails.
Options: count in the route over several reads (PostgREST caps rows at 1000 and cannot sum over joins) or one SQL function; revenue from prompt_purchases (dead) or from the payment ledgers.
Decision: one function, enki_stats(p_since, p_sort, p_limit) (migrations/2026-10-29-enki-stats.sql = sql-to-run/44), behind GET /api/analytics/enki, public like the Hall of Fame (numbers and handles). What counts:
- Accounts deleted, not active or banned (lib/hidden-owners.ts's rule) drop out of every figure; the ranking also leaves out who hid from the leaderboard.
- Artist revenue = the artist's share of each delivered paid render in mainnet USDC, gross: licence credits owed to artists (x402, withheld intent shares), intent captures paid directly (no credit, a mainnet generation), escrow settlements (delivered units at the original share). Never devnet (every escrow row live is devnet, so $0 today), voided, released or undelivered payments, nor a creator paying for renders of their own prompt (the account that rendered, for a credit; the paying wallet, for an intent).
- Views = prompts.views, a counter without time: all time only, null in a week or a month and in the last day. Image views are tracked nowhere.
- Posts are dated by a new generated_images.published_at, set by a trigger when an image first goes public (the first time is kept); the 2 images public before SQL 44 get their created_at.
- Generated images = renders not uploaded, not deleted. Likes and comments count only on prompts and images that are not deleted (VERIFIED live: today's 3 likes and 1 comment are on deleted prompts, so both read 0).
- The ranking is public activity only (prompts, posts, revenue, views, likes, comments, followers): a person's private render count is an Enki total, never their column.
Evidence: VERIFIED: enki-stats-migration.test.ts 7 (PGlite: each rule above in and out, the trigger, ranking, limit, grants, runs twice, rollback), enki-stats-route.test.ts 5; in-memory mutants over SQL, route and UI: first 60 (57 killed; an anchor typo, a fixture without a private render, and an escrow state filter that the table's CHECK makes redundant, deleted), then 78 after the review fixes (75 killed; a referrer who was also the payer, fixed in the fixture; a redundant `?? null`, deleted; an unknown period not pinned, test added), every handled one then killed; tsc exit 0. Independent review (3 lenses, each verified by a skeptic): confirmed and fixed self-buys, likes and comments on deleted content, private render counts on the ranking, a link for "unnamed", stale figures under a new period; refuted a lost credit write (Enki's own ledger repairs it by hand) and agent accounts as users (full accounts by design). INFERRED: cost is one scan of the counted tables per request, fine at today's size (users 39, generated_images 56, prompts 72).
Revert: git revert of this commit; the SQL's rollback at its end.

### DEC-2026-10-29-518: views by day as daily counters per prompt and image; "watched" means opened
Context: Kev 2026-10-29: "views by day, i feel like this is needed as views for posts are also being recorded. find a slim and efficient way to do that, would be great to know what prompts and images have been watched so that we know who gets most attention". VERIFIED live: image views were recorded nowhere; prompts had two counters without time (views = a card seen in the feed, 484; opens = opened, 174), deduped per viewer in one instance's memory for 30 and 10 minutes.
Options: an event log (prompt_analytics_events exists, 0 rows: a row per view, grows without bound, needs aggregation on read); daily counters per item (one row per kind, day and item, upserted); counters on the rows only (no days).
Decision: daily counters: view_days(kind, day, target_id, n), migrations/2026-10-29-view-days.sql = sql-to-run/49. The two prompt counter functions keep their arguments and also upsert the day's row, so the feed's routes stay; count_image_opens(p_images, p_viewer) counts an image opened large, public renders only, never the viewer's own; POST /api/images/views takes a batch, deduped per viewer and image for a day on the instance, guest allowed. "Watched" = opened (a prompt opened, an image shown large), not a card scrolled past: an impression says where the feed placed it, an open says someone wanted it. The opens counted before the table sit on 1970-01-01 ("before 2026-10-29"), so all time includes them and no period does. The browser counts once per UTC day per image (lib/ui/view-beacon.ts: localStorage, memory without it, batched every 3 s with keepalive); a script can still inflate counts, as before. enki_stats counts views per owner and period and ranks by them (the Views column no longer all-time only), and lists the ten prompts and ten images opened most in the period: listed prompts and public images only, never 18+, never of a hidden or opted-out account. The three counter functions become service role only (they were callable by anyone). Not done in this commit: the image UI's stage and viewer call the beacon once the references piece has left useImageViewModel.ts; the prompt open moves from the feed card into the prompt view (so profile and deep-link opens count) as its own change; the /i share page counts nothing (bots read it); creator examples count as the prompt's open.
Evidence: VERIFIED: view-days-migration.test.ts 6 (PGlite over enki-stats + artist-earnings: the days written by each function, own/private/upload refused, the 'before' bucket once, totals and board per period, watched lists with every exclusion, grants, rollback), view-beacon.test.ts 3, images-views-route.test.ts 3; in-memory mutants 26 then 12: 36 killed, 1 redundant WHERE deleted (the joins already named the kinds), 1 test gap closed (a repeat after the flush without storage). INFERRED: a day row per item keeps the table at (items × days with activity) rows, a scan per request is fine at Enki's size.
Revert: git revert of this commit; the SQL's rollback at its end.

### DEC-2026-10-29-525: uploaded references stay in the picker until deleted: saved privately per account (SQL 51)
Context: Kev 2026-10-29: "the images uploaded via ref image uploading must remain in that image upload UI until i delete them, this must be the database of uploaded referenced images". An upload lived only in this visit's state. A reference is image-checked only at render (app/api/generate-image/route.ts:559-603, checkImageBytes) and stored publicly only after delivery (route.ts:1155-1163); generate-free refuses references (route.ts:69).
Options: (a) the render's public Vercel Blob file (references/<user>/<sha256>.<ext>, reference-images.ts:66 access "public"); (b) a private Supabase bucket behind signed links (the DM pattern, lib/dm.ts:74); (c) a paid image check on every save.
Decision: (b). POST /api/references takes the picker's data URL (PNG/JPEG/WebP, bytes matching the named type, at most REQUEST_MAX_BYTES), counts the account's kept rows first and stops with 503 when the count is missing (SQL 51 not run: postgrest-js turns the missing table's empty 404 into a 204 with no count), so nothing is stored before SQL 51 or at the cap. It stores <user>/<sha256>.<ext> and a 256 px WebP tile in the private bucket "reference-uploads" and upserts on (user_id, content_hash), clearing deleted_at. GET returns the owner's kept rows with links valid for 1 h (the picker re-reads every 30 min) plus deleted hashes. DELETE marks the row deleted and removes both files. The picker shows unsaved uploads, then saved tiles with a ×, then earlier render references whose stored hash is neither saved nor deleted. A saved tile is read without re-drawing (useReferenceReads raw), so the render's checked public copy has the same hash and stays hidden.
Moderation: no check per save; the check still runs at the render that sends the picture. Residual risk: Enki keeps unchecked pictures privately until a render (child-safety content possible); an owner can pass a signed link on, good for up to an hour; a deleted account's rows go, its files stay (private). Open for Kev: add the image check per save (a paid call per upload) or keep it at render.
Evidence: VERIFIED live by the builder/fixer, read-only: HEAD count on the missing table {"status":204,"count":null,"error":null} (postgrest-js 2.103.3, index.cjs:384-386); GET 404 PGRST205; users.id uuid pk; 13/13 generation_reference_images rows named references/<user uuid>/<sha256>.<ext>; buckets profiles and generations only. VERIFIED by me: the 77 test files that read a changed file (expert-doc excluded, busy in another change) `77 passed (77)`, `956 passed (956)`; the fixer's mutant spec re-run: 96 of 97 killed, the 97th did not load (a syntax error in the spec), re-run in loadable form ("old && {" → "true && {"): killed; tsc clean. A review pass found 4 defects in the first build (files stored before SQL 51, public unchecked links, a deleted upload back among earlier renders, a second copy on re-pick), all fixed. Not seen in a browser (access gate).
Revert: git revert of the commit; SQL 51's rollback (drops table and cap function; empty and delete the bucket on the dashboard).

### DEC-2026-10-29-532: the Full prompt document is typed into where it stands; the view never turns into the raw words
Context: Kev 2026-10-29: "i dont get why the textfeld changes to that "reference image" thing, lass doch einfach die view mit den images and just lemme change texts without the UI actually changing at all, it even changes to the variable names which is off, shouldnt be the case, i gotta see the entire prompt." Since c9c11ff2 (DEC-526) a click on a word flipped m.view to "text": the raw PromptMirror with "Reference image 1" and "[name]"; a multi-choice or slider token flipped too.
Options: keep the raw editor behind a gesture; one contentEditable for the whole document with tokens as atoms; one editable run per text segment, tokens untouched.
Decision: each text segment is one contentEditable="plaintext-only" run (.iv-run) around its word spans (kept for image drops). The browser's caret goes where the click is; a blur after input commits that segment's slice into m.text (U+00A0 → space), Enter commits, Esc puts it back and stops there, IME composition is left alone. A typed "[mood]" or "Reference image 2" becomes a token on commit. Empty runs stand where a token opens or ends the text or two tokens meet, so words can go there too. Every part is keyed by its text and its count among equal texts (not by index), with a per-part redraw counter after an edited blur, so React never patches nodes the browser rewrote and a click from one run into the next keeps its focus. An image drag blurs a focused run first and finds the image by key at the drop. Multi-choice and slider tokens open their VariableField in the panel under the words. "Reset to the artist's wording" sits in the document's tools when m.edited and not blank. On touch screens the document is 16 px (iOS zooms on a focus under 16). Nothing calls setView("text") any more.
Evidence: VERIFIED: the 22 test files that read PromptPanel, image-view.css, image-view-mobile.css or kit-media `22 passed (22)`, `321 passed (321)`; the full suite `449 passed (449)`, `5372 passed (5372)`; the fixer's 33 in-memory mutants re-run by me, `survivors: 0 of 33`; tsc clean. REPORTED by the builder/fixer/reviewers: the real PromptPanel bundled into a headless Edge harness with real mouse, key and touch events: builder 28/28, double edit 7/7, fixes + touch 26/26, no React errors; a review found 18 issues (a phone drag after typing crashed with insertBefore or lost the typing; a drop after typing did nothing; no place for words after a final token; index keys lost the next click's typing; no IME guard; iOS zoom; test gaps), 13 fixed, 3 rejected. Not seen on 3008 (access gate), not on Safari/iOS/Firefox.
Open for Kev: (1) a [variable] cannot be removed from the words any more (the raw editor was the only way); recommended: Backspace at a run's start removes the token before it, Delete at its end the one after. (2) The Reset link also shows after only adding a photo (m.edited is set by growText); recommended: show it only when the words changed.
Revert: git revert of the commit.

### DEC-2026-10-30-585: Kev's 18 holds however a render came in: works keep the first 18 it reached (corrects DEC-571)
Context: Kev 2026-10-30: "max 18 communities pro werk". DEC-571 counted a render's prompt's communities into the 18 only in PUT /api/communities/links, at the time of that write. A prompt linked later (by its creator, not the render's owner) took a render with 18 of its own to 21 in community_works, and its owner's next save of the list she saw was refused with 409 (review 2026-10-30, REVPROBE1).
Options: refuse the prompt's link (would let one render block its prompt's creator); copy the cap into each write path (still breaks on a later prompt link); hold it where works are read (chosen).
Decision: SQL 54 adds the view community_reach (every way a render reaches a community: 'link', 'prompt', 'post', with when that way began, opt-outs and hides left out). community_works keeps a render in the first 18 communities it reached, by (linked_at, community_id); earlier ones keep their places, a later prompt link waits until a place frees. lib/communities/server.ts placesOf reads the same order, so GET /api/communities/links shows where the render really is. PUT opts a render out only of a prompt community it shows in (or has a row for): saving the list as shown changes nothing. A Showroom post's communities take places too but are the post's to set (not on the render's list).
Evidence: VERIFIED: communities-migration.test.ts "keeps a render in the first 18 communities it reached ..." and communities-routes.test.ts "keeps a render in 18 however it came ..."; mutants (mutmem, in memory) "SQL: works not capped at 18", "SQL: the latest 18 kept, not the first", "placesOf: no cap", "PUT: opts out of what never showed", "itemCommunities: a post's places on the render's list" killed. INFERRED: the view's cost (a correlated count per row over the render's ways, indexable by image_id/prompt_id/post_id); not measured.
Revert: git revert of the commit (SQL 54 is a file only until Kev runs it).

### DEC-2026-10-30-593: Creators are read by search, not by their timeline, with cursors per creator
Context: The timeline walk bills every post an account made (the newest 800). Kev: "ja 400$ ist extrem viel, gibts günstigere wege?"
Options: timeline walk (legacy); recent plus full-archive search `from:<handle> (words) has:images -is:retweet -is:reply [min_likes:n]`, billed per matching post (chosen).
Decision:
- Phase "new": since newest_id. The recent endpoint while newest_id is younger than 6 days, the full archive after that.
- Phase "back": the full archive, until oldest_id, with start_time = since_days.
- A "new" phase cut short keeps gap_top and gap_low and resumes below gap_low.
- An empty first look back sets newest_id from a snowflake of the round's start.
- The dry stop applies to the look back only. A changed search resets every cursor, and X bills the re-read.
- Long posts are read from note_tweet.
- Every post must carry the creator's X id (author_id). Another id stops the round ("@h is another X account now") and files nothing.
Evidence:
- REPORTED (design agent, docs.x.com): full-archive search is open to pay-per-use at $0.005 per post read.
- VERIFIED (workflow agents): review round 1 reproduced four cursor bugs with a fake X (the handle changed hands, a creator dead after an empty look back, the dry stop in the new phase, a starved backlog). After the fixes the probes were re-run: PROBE-EMPTY Play 2 `"found":1`; PROBE-HANDLE `submission of X author B's post: []`.
- Not determined, all of it shows at the first live Play: whether X accepts a time-built since_id; since_id and until_id together; min_likes on pay-per-use; tweet.fields vs post.fields.
Revert: git revert of the commit.

### DEC-2026-10-30-594: The prompt is cut verbatim; the model only points at its start and end
Context: Kev: "akkurat den prompt rausfiltern". A prompt sits in the post text, in an image alt, or in the author's reply.
Options: the model rewrites the prompt; heuristics only; heuristics first, then gpt-6-luna for unsure posts, used only to find positions (chosen).
Decision:
- Order: the post text first. A "Prompt:" label or block counts only as one paragraph with no second "Prompt N:" and no call-to-action tail.
- Then a reply hint: the author's replies in the conversation are read, which is billed. Then the alt texts.
- A quoted passage always goes to the model.
- cutVerbatim takes one span of the cleaned source, from the model's start words to its end words, at least 40 characters. So every prompt is a subsequence of what the creator posted.
- If the model saw only the first 4,000 characters of the source it picked, the post is too_long: refused, and visible in the Posts CSV.
- Model down: unchecked.
Evidence: VERIFIED (workflow agents): the distill tests assert isSubsequence(prompt, rawSource) on every path. The review probes, re-run after the fix: JSON, tail and two-label posts give `"kind":"unsure"`; the title post gives `{"kind":"reply"}`; PROBE-LONG gives `{"ok":false,"why":"too_long"}`.
Revert: git revert of the commit.

### DEC-2026-11-02-05: Start over takes back a creator's distill failed and reply missing marks
Context: Failed posts stayed marked as read in hunter_posts and were skipped as "seen" for good, even after Start over. Agreed proposal: Start over also removes this creator's failure marks, so the next Play tries them again; settled outcomes stay. Start over spends nothing; the next Play pays about $0.0007 per retried post.
Options: delete the marks at Start over (chosen, agreed); a separate "Retry failed" button; keep the marks and let a Play ignore them.
Decision: restartCreator deletes hunter_posts rows of the handle with outcome distill_failed or reply_missing, after the cursors moved, so a mark never goes while the cursors are still past its post. A failed delete answers 500; pressing again finishes it. Button title and confirm say it. A search change (saveCreator) keeps RESTART alone: it was not asked for and would spend without saying so. One more change for the dry stop: a seen find now ends the streak as it did at its first read. Without it the retried failures of a creator counted as "in a row" across its old finds, because a seen post touched nothing: live, with dry_after 30 on all 8 creators, one creator has 9 failures with at most 2 between finds and two have 30 and 38 in a row. A seen no_prompt or a link waiting in line leaves the streak.
What reads these rows: takePage's seen check (the point of this); the log and the CSV, where a removed mark is gone until the next Play writes the post's new outcome; loadCreators reads only 'waiting'. posts_read, found and spend are on hunter_accounts, not these rows: found rises once per retried find (test), posts_read rises by the re-read as every Start over always did.
Residual risk: (1) a link added by hand that failed and that the creator's search does not return loses its log line and is not retried: use Add link again; not determined how many of the 95 are such. (2) 30 retries that fail in a row stop dry as the brake is meant to, the marks below it are gone and those posts wait until Start over reaches them; each such Start over pays about $0.012 in distills, more for a higher dry_after. (3) $0.0007 is the agreed figure, not a measurement: a failed distill is $0.00041 (HUNT_PRICES.distill), a retry that succeeds with four pictures up to $0.0016 (MODEL_USD_PER_POST_MAX); the spend cap holds either way. (4) No Play was run: 78 distill failures may fail again, whether they do is not determined.
Evidence: VERIFIED live read, outcomes and rows with a submission: `distill_failed n 78 withSubmission 0`, `reply_missing n 17 withSubmission 0`, `queued n 135 withSubmission 135`, `duplicate 5`, `too_long 2`, `waiting 1`; 95 marks on 6 of 8 handles. Files touching the changed sources: `Tests 364 passed (364)`. Blind spot: the page was read as source, not pressed in a browser.

### DEC-2026-11-02-09: A word meets a tag as the vocabulary spells it or as that word's plural; no stemmer; one-word aliases that mostly mean something else are gone
Context: Kev 2026-11-02: "Generate" gave the tag "general", "valley" and "reading" sat on a logo prompt with no such thing. Measured now, word by word, over 279 live prompts and 6 waiting finds. Two causes. (1) The Porter stemmer in the matcher: 706 of 2,170 word-to-tag pairs, 4,754 of 21,776 hits, came only through it, and it merges words of different meaning: generate, generous, generic, generation -> general; element -> elemental; iconic -> icon; expression -> expressionism; orientation -> orientalism; status -> statue; even -> evening; added, adding -> advertisement (synonym "ad"); animal -> anime (synonym "animation"); read, reads -> reading; glass -> glasses; leave -> leaves. (2) One-word synonyms and bare tags whose common meaning in prompts is another one, read in their live contexts: "figure" -> figurine (42 prompts), "senior" (a senior designer) -> elderly person, "director" (art director) -> filmmaker, "space" -> outer space, "square" -> plaza, "present" -> gift, "official" -> formal, "still" -> calm, "atmosphere" -> misty mood; bare "key" (anime key visual), "uniform" (uniform background), "band" (color band), "running" (running along), "reading" (reading direction: 0 of 14 meant the act), "camera" and "studio" (the how, Kev's rule). "valleys" on the logo prompt: 12 uses in 4 prompts, all folds and tones (fold valleys, tonal valleys), 1 real "valley".
Options: patch single words in a stop list (stemmer stays, every new word can do it again); an inflection-only stem, Porter step 1 (keeps read -> reading, added -> ad, spacing -> space, parking -> park); spelled words plus their regular plural (chosen); a model (paid, Kev 2026-09-24: "kostenlos").
Decision: lib/search/tags.ts indexes each term as spelled and its regular plural on the last word, spelled terms first. One way: "dragons" meets "dragon", but "glass" does not meet "glasses". A phrase also matches with its last word's plural dropped, as a phrase has no second meaning ("warm color" = "warm colors"). Vocabulary, lib/search/vocabulary.json: the forms the stemmer reached that do mean the tag are now written out, after reading the 363 lost pairs one by one (metal -> metallic, printed -> print, branded -> branding, stands -> standing, jump -> jumping, the singulars of plural tags: wire, pipe, glove...). 39 one-word synonyms removed. "hidden" deleted (0 of 12 a mood). New how-terms own their words: folds and valleys ("valleys"), render engine, clear coat, canvas (Canva is software, a canvas is not); texture map and four more join normal map. New subjects coat and tank top, as the lost "trench coat" and "tank" were really these. Bare "general" stays: the word itself occurs 0 times live, only the stem hit it. Stored tags do not change: no write, no sealed preview touched; Kev's "go Prompts" has not been given.

(2) A word's other meaning is only fixed where it was seen: left as they read mixed: model (65 uses, some "3d model"), ring, bar, face, hand, feet, map, ink, charcoal. A paid body's bigrams were read only in this process and not recorded. (3) Left unrestored on purpose, may be a correct tag lost in some prompts: sits -> sitting (mostly "the logo sits"), falls -> falling, gear -> gears, weave -> weaving, symbolic -> symbolism, photographer -> photograph, industry -> industrial, modern -> modernism. (4) The waiting finds' sealed tags hold the old false hits, and the backfill's and Generate's formula feeds the sealed or model tags back in: a stale "toned" stays until a retag recomputes without them (4 of 6 finds keep 1 to 6 stale tags in a backfill). ### DEC-2026-11-02-14: A chain counts only once its end is known, and a post's own prompt comes before following
Context: review of DEC-12's follow code, with throwaway PGlite proofs I reread against the source; each failing case holds (REPORTED by the review, INFERRED by reading fx-api.ts:171-184 and manual-link.ts:63). (1) A chain whose last hop is a comment answered `reply`, though followChain's own doc quotes Kev: "in the core prompt in one of the comments was that prompt". (2) readStatus returned null for a deleted post and for a failed read alike, so a post quoting a deleted one was follow_failed at every Start over. (3) An added link ignored chain.broken and filed the forward's own words under the forwarder. (4) A chain cut at CHAIN_MAX or by a loop returned a forward as its core. (5) A text-only core was queued with no picture, though the forward has one; 0 of 199 approved finds have no picture live.
Options for (5): the nearest forward's picture (chosen); a mark so the admin sees it has none (a new HuntFacts field and panel code, and the admin still has no picture to publish); nothing.
Decision: readStatus says "gone" for a final 404 or 401, null for a failed read. followChain returns broken for a failed read or a cut chain, and gone when the post it leads to is deleted or private and the last hop has no words of its own (promptLike and not defers); with words of its own that hop is the core. A post that links itself forwards nothing. A core that is a comment gives way to the post it answers when the author is the same, with the comment as the given reply and the parent as the chain's last hop; another author's comment or a gone parent stays a comment, which a Play reads as `reply`, no find. In a Play, gone reads the post as its own; broken stays follow_failed. An added link or a link put in line answers 503 for broken and 404 for gone, and nothing is listed. A core with no picture shows the nearest forward's, its alt text dropped so it is no source of the prompt; never on a video-only core, and a comment's own picture goes first.
Residual risk: (1) A 404 four times in a row reads as deleted and is final: the timeline answered about one 404 in four live (fx-api.ts:48), the status endpoint's rate not determined; 401 and 404 on v2 are INFERRED from the v1 reader (lib/editor/post-import.ts:74-75), not seen live. (2) A chain over five posts stays follow_failed through every Start over: it can never be read to its end. (3) Kev should know: the forward's picture shows under the core's author, in the queue for a person to look at, since a chain's find is never published at once. (4) A text-only core whose own reply has a picture read through the reader takes the forward's picture first, only a given comment's goes before it. (5) A comment of a comment is not climbed further.
Evidence: VERIFIED in memory mutants C1-C30, baseline `98 passed, 0 failed, 0 not loaded`, 27 killed; C16, C26, C30 survived, one case each added, then `survivors: 0 of 3` and C26 in a run of its own. Live read: `approved 199 with zero photos 0`, `pending 6 with chain posts > 1 0 with zero photos 1`. Blind spot: no live FxTwitter read and no live Play; stubs are shaped as earlier live reads.
Also, from the same review, own prompt first (next commit, 2026-11-02): a post whose own words could be a prompt (ownWords) goes to the model before following, and is followed only if the model finds none, reusing forward(): a short unlabelled prompt above a quote was lost, a hit found before DEC-12 (REPORTED `[C-before-feature]` found 1, `[C-with-feature]` found 0). A post that defers, or has too few words, is followed first as before. In recipe and manual modes there is no model, so such words stay the creator's, queued for a person; a forward with long chatter there is queued as its words, and its core needs Add link. A core of the creator's own that gives no find no longer lends the post its outcome: its row is written and the post is read as its own, one more model call. A chain's core of the creator's own is always queued, like another's, since a chain bypasses the search filters and the comment above said so.
Residual risk of it: a forward with 40 or more characters of chatter costs one more distill, about $0.0004, and the model could take chatter for a prompt; Purple8419's real forward is of that kind (manual-link.test.ts:111). Not measured live, as no Play was run.
Evidence of it: VERIFIED mutants O1-O8, baseline `77 passed, 0 failed, 0 not loaded`, O6 survived, a case added, then killed.
Revert: revert these two commits, the later first.

### DEC-2026-11-02-20: A false alarm on a child-safety image: one logged human decision, one exact checksum, the hunter's import only
Context: an imported creator's find (@aurenvossvt) was refused for a picture judged minor_sexualised 0.85, and overturning its case changes nothing: an import asks the judges again. Kev's go for the Auren case: the owner looks, overturns, and exactly that image, by checksum of the judged bytes, counts as reviewed. Correction to the brief: it says the case is pending. So overturned alone must never count, and the button must stay open on an already overturned image case.
Options: count an overturned event as the clearance, no table (rejected: that very row would then pass unseen); hash the bytes anew or unseal the evidence at the press (rejected: the case already holds it, see Evidence); lift inside checkImageBytes for every caller (rejected: every route would need to opt out); a table, the existing hash, the lift in judgeImport for surface prompt-hunter alone (chosen).
Decision: table image_clearances (SQL 61, pending): sha256, event_id, cleared_by, cleared_at, revoked_at, revoked_by, one standing per case. The overturn of a csam image-check event (lib/moderation/image-clearance): moderation owner only, their own reveal of that case's image in artist_text_reveals (prompt_id null), else 403 "You cannot clear what you have not looked at. Reveal the image first."; then the clearance, then the event; if the event's write fails the clearance is undone. An uphold by any admin revokes by checksum, so another case of the same bytes takes it back too. The hash and the count go into the admin log through the route's answer (audit OUTCOME: cleared, revoked). checkImage keeps its verdict and adds `otherwise`, what verdictOf says with the two minor rules out of the way, under the same one-judge-down rule; checkImageBytes takes the worst of every view and refuses a moving image in it. judgeImport with surface prompt-hunter uses `otherwise` when imageCleared(sha256(got.buf)); no new case then. Defaults I picked for Kev: any admin may take a clearance back (only makes it stricter); a non-owner admin can no longer overturn an image case, he can mark it reviewed; the import that passes writes no log row of its own, the clearance is the logged decision.
Evidence: VERIFIED the hash is over the judged bytes: lib/moderation/image-case.ts:78 `prompt_hash: createHash("sha256").update(ctx.bytes)` and judge-post passes `bytes: got.buf`, `sha256(got.buf)` is the same digest; `git log -L78,78` shows only 0cc2a2a7, the commit that made cases; prompt_hash is NOT NULL (the test's null insert: `null value in column "prompt_hash" ... violates not-null constraint`). ### DEC-2026-11-02-22: The bot guard on free renders: Turnstile in the route, then a daily cap and one per hashed address in SQL
Context: Kev (2026-10-30): "ich will auch nicht, dass bots über x402 free generations haben bei mir. only humans are allowed to have 1 for free" (a founder lost $4k to bots farming free credits). Decided then: Turnstile on the free claim, the server checks the token in the route, because a bot calls the API directly; base build a global daily cap + Turnstile + one per hashed IP a day; stronger proof only if the cap fills regularly. The account's two ever (DEC-2026-10-31-01, SQL 57) stay as they are.
Options: (a) counters per day and bucket (release needs both keys and a decrement that can go below zero after midnight); (b) one row per claim, as free_generation_claims, released by id; (c) the caps inside claim_free_generation (ties two migrations and a pending SQL 57 together, and the caps must come before the model checks, the account's claim after them).
Decision: (b). SQL 63 (pending, Kev runs it): free_render_claims(day, ip_bucket), claim_free_render(bucket, day limit, ip limit) under one transaction lock across all accounts, the day read after the lock. The day's cap is counted first, so a full day is said as one. Default 200 a UTC day, FREE_RENDERS_PER_DAY overrides, a broken value counts as unset, 0 closes the day. One per hashed address a UTC day: a shared office or mobile network gets one a day between them and a person's second free image waits for the next day; that is the accepted cost. Unknown address or a missing AUTH_PEPPER: one shared bucket, no bypass. Hash as lib/ip-hash's hashIp, the address as the rate limiter reads it (getClientIp in lib/rate-limit, exported for this): lib/ip-hash's own reader takes the left-most x-forwarded-for entry, which the caller writes, and would have opened a new bucket per request wherever the platform does not overwrite it. Each claim deletes earlier days' rows, so a hash lives one day. free_render_full_days holds no address and stays, as the record of how often the cap fills, which is Kev's measure for a stronger proof. A day's first refusal inserts its row and only that answer sends the one mail, to OPS_ALERT_EMAILS by sendMail: no helper existed beyond sendMail (the cron's tell is private to its route). A mail that fails is not sent again that day; it is logged by the mailer. No exemption for admins: the code exempts nobody ("Every account is capped, including team roles", free-quota.ts).
Before SQL 63: PGRST202 or 42883 from the call lets the render through on today's limits with one warning per server process. An outage answers 503, any other error or a malformed reply refuses (nothing granted on a bad answer).
Evidence: VERIFIED live, read-only, script deleted: `free_render_claims { status: 404, code: 'PGRST205' }`, `free_render_full_days { status: 404, code: 'PGRST205' }`, `missing function { status: 404, code: 'PGRST202' }`, `free_generation_claims columns { status: 200, code: null, rows: 1 }`. Correction: my first read used a head request and answered `{ status: 204, code: null }` on those absent tables, which shows nothing; the plain read above is the measurement. VERIFIED lib/__tests__/free-render-caps.test.ts on PGlite with and without the migration `17 passed (17)`; mutants "survivors: 0 of 33". Blind spots: PGlite is one session, so eight parallel claims at a cap of three ran in turn and the lock was never contended: the count is proven, the lock only by a pin on its line; SQL 63 was not run on the live database; a real Vercel x-real-ip was not seen (the rate limiter's comment and Vercel's behaviour are REPORTED).
Revert: revert this commit; rollback of SQL 63 at the file's end.
The route (its own commit): session, the admin gate, the step-up, then Turnstile, then the caps, all inside the existing `if (quotaUserId)` and before screenFirst, checkPrompt, moderate and the account's claim. The step-up asks first because a token is good once and a step-up refusal must not spend it. A finally gives the day's place back on every answer but a delivered image, so no later return can forget it. Turnstile (lib/turnstile.ts): JSON POST to siteverify with the secret and the token, 5 s; success true passes, success false refuses (403), except internal-error and the secret's own two codes, which say the check itself is broken. Missing secret, no answer, a 5xx, not JSON, or those codes: "paused" (503) when VERCEL_ENV is production, elsewhere skipped with one warning. The client's address is not sent to Cloudflare (optional in their API; less data). hostname and action are not compared: one widget, one use, the widget's hostnames are set in the dashboard. Answers: 429 for both caps. x402 has no free path and gets no guard: its route names neither the free route, the claim nor the free host and refuses every host but gemini, wavespeed and openai before money moves. CSP: there is none to extend. vitest.setup.ts throws on every real socket and needs no change.
Residuals, reported not changed: only an admin reaches this route today (mayUseFreeHost), so today the guard stands in front of Kev's own tests: with SQL 63 one render per network a day, and in production no free render without the keys. An account with both images used still costs one moderation call per try, as today, because its claim comes after the checks; it now needs a fresh token for each try.
Evidence (route): VERIFIED lib/__tests__/free-render-guard-route.test.ts and turnstile.test.ts `baseline: 41 passed, 0 failed, 0 not loaded`, mutants "survivors: 0 of 32"; every test naming the changed files `Test Files  46 passed (46)`, `Tests  954 passed (954)`; tsc clean, check-imports "5 files, 0 unresolved"; `grep -c "claim_free_generation\|generate-free\|Pollinations\|freeGeneration" app/api/x402/generate/route.ts` = 0, app/api/x402/generate/route.ts:490 lists the hosts; `grep -rln Content-Security-Policy` over ts, tsx, json and mjs outside node_modules finds none.
