### DEC-2026-11-02-24: A take-back reaches what the clearance let through: a waiting find at its publish, a published prompt by a takedown
Context: review of DEC-2026-11-02-20 (high). takeBackClearance touched only image_clearances: a find queued while cleared stayed publishable for its token's 14 days, a published prompt stayed live, no link led from a checksum to either, and the admin panel said "This image counts as unreviewed again". REPORTED by the review's bench: `B2 approve 200 {"ok":true,"published":1}`, `B2 stored after revoke 1 sha is the case's true`.
Options for the find: a `cleared` list in the preview, re-asked at the publish (only what the import knew at the time); ask the checksums' cases at every publish, a $0 read (chosen: also catches a case filed after the import, and needs nothing in the token). Options for the prompt: a list in hunt_submissions.preview found by a jsonb query with minted_prompt_id (no schema change, but marked at the two import paths, and a publish racing a take-back stays open); a note table in SQL 61, written before the listing (chosen); name the prompt in the answer only (leaves an upheld child-safety image on sale).
Decision: POST /api/prompt, for any imported token, reads casedImages (image cases on its checksums, whatever their state, then the standing clearances): a held one answers 422 PHOTOS_REFUSED before anything is stored; an unreadable read 503 PHOTOS_UNCHECKED. Bytes under a standing clearance get a row in image_clearance_prompts before the listing, then the clearance is asked again: a take-back before the note refuses the listing, one after it finds the prompt, and the listing's existing `.is("delisted_at", null)` keeps it down. takeBackClearance takes those prompts down as a report's delist does (is_listed false, delisted_at), and names them: answer and admin log get `unlisted` and `prompts`. Defaults I picked for Kev: the takedown is automatic on any admin's uphold, because a true positive on sale is the worse error and a relist stays an admin's step; a later re-clear does not put a prompt back; a failed takedown answers 500 with the clearance already gone, the case not yet upheld, and pressing again finishes it (the takedown does not depend on anything being left to revoke).
Evidence: VERIFIED live read-only, script deleted: `image_clearance_prompts {"status":404,"code":"PGRST205"}`, `automod_events cols {"status":200}`, `prompts cols {"status":200}`, `artist_text_reveals cols {"status":200}`. VERIFIED lib/__tests__/prompt-import-clearance.test.ts (new, the real POST /api/prompt on PGlite with the real migrations, a real sealed token) and image-clearance.test.ts `baseline: 61 passed, 0 failed, 0 not loaded`; mutants 24 of 26 killed on the first run: `.eq("category", "csam")` proved redundant with isImageCase and was deleted, `note table open` survived because PGlite has no default privileges, and now grants first and re-runs the file (killed). Blind spots: the approve button's path was read, not run, from publishApproved through publishImported to this route (publishImported is covered by its own test, the failed publish going back to pending by admin-hunter); the takedown hides the prompt, its pictures stay at their blob URLs, as with a report's delist; a prompt written before the note table existed cannot exist, because no clearance can stand before SQL 61; PGlite is one session, so the race was run by a take-back inside the store step, not by two connections; the prompt's row stays, unlisted, when the listing is refused.
Not done: the approver still is not told a find holds a cleared image; the panel's toast stays "Clearance taken back." and the count is in the answer and the log.
Revert: revert this commit; SQL 61's copy in sql-to-run then needs the migration's old text.

### DEC-2026-11-02-26: An x402 refusal to a request with a payment says nothing of that payment
Context: review of 7d5760b9 (low). requirementsFor refuses before simulatePayment and paymentLanded, so the retry of a payment that settled, on a prompt switched off in between, was told "Nothing was charged." and lost the 409 that carries its transaction. Not changed, reported to Kev.

### DEC-2026-11-03-05: A creator's shelf sorts by performance on the server and pages to its end
Context: Kev, 2026-11-03: "fix the released wand, das soll auch son endless scroller sein ofc mit den performances sichtbar and below the bar a sort by performance und date und auch nen filter nach categories, generatoren." Server part. Uses, likes and views as decided in the task: renders by others (DEC-2026-11-03-03), prompts.like_count, prompts.opens. Nothing in the prompts row holds uses, so the order needs a read of generations. A failed read of ?creator= answered 200 with no prompts, which is an empty wall; a failed handle lookup read as an unknown handle, the same.
Options: order in SQL through a view or function (new SQL for Kev to run, for a shelf of 119); read the ranking columns, then the page's cards by id (a second read, a smaller first one); read the whole filtered shelf with the card columns on the query that already carries every filter, sort it here and slice (chosen: no second list of filters that can drift).
Decision: sortBy=performance with ?creator= pages through generations and the shelf, sorts by uses, likes, views, on a read ordered created_at desc, id (the sort is stable, so that read is the tie-break), and slices offset and limit. Without a creator it answers as newest and echoes newest. ?stats=1 with ?creator= adds stats; a failed count gives null on that page, and answers 500 on the performance sort. Reads page until one comes back empty, so a max-rows below 1000 cannot cut them either, at one more read each. Defaults I chose beyond the task: any ?creator= read that fails now answers an error, also by date, and also a failed handle lookup (the only caller, ProfileView.tsx, already throws on !res.ok; the feed without a creator keeps its empty answer); a shelf's pages also order by id, so equal dates cannot swap between pages, while the feed's read stays as it was. ?category= maps a chip's "marketing" to ENKI_CATEGORIES' "Marketing"; any other label goes through as sent.
Move this to SQL at a shelf of 1000 listed prompts or 10000 renders by others of one creator. Every page of the wall rereads the whole shelf, with no cache. VERIFIED measured against live, medians of 5: one read of 119 rows 122 ms and 140585 bytes, one read of 279 rows 178 ms and 283087 bytes, so 0.35 ms and about 1 KB a row. The route's first page: `performance 772`, `newest, stats 650`, `newest, no stats 578` ms, so 122 ms for the sort today. INFERRED from that rate, not run: about 430 ms and 1 MB for each page at 1000 rows. The largest shelf today is 119.

### DEC-2026-11-03-14: No Play lists anyone: a forward to someone not on the list only marks the post
Context: Kev, 2026-11-03: "warum sollte ein fremder in der liste landen, wenn ich die doch alle prüfe und somit keine fremde dort auftauchen?" Correction to DEC-2026-11-02-15, whose default listed a stranger, with an Enki account and a model call, when the post they wrote held a prompt. What was wrong: it treated "holds a prompt" as enough to list someone, though Kev vets every creator himself. The review it came from only asked why a "gm" listed someone, so the fix tested the words of the post and never asked who may decide. DEC-15's residual risks (1), (2) and (3) on strangers no longer apply, nor does (5) for a stranger.
Options: storage of who the post leads to: a new column by SQL (needs a run first, and a code path that survives it missing, as prompts.source_reach showed); a line in admin_actions as hunter.knownLink (playCreator has no request or gate to record with, and the post's row would say something else); the handle inside hunter_posts.outcome, leads_to:<handle> (chosen, no SQL). Options for the mark's scope: everything that is not a free exit (chosen, as the task says, "unsure" included, no model); only a sure prompt (Kev would never hear of an unsure one).
Decision: in forward(), an author not on hunter_accounts gets no upsert, no Play, no account and no model call. A reply, a video-only post or a post where locatePrompt finds nothing, their replies read once for free, reads the forwarder's post as its own, as before. Anything else marks the forwarder's post leads_to:<handle>. It is neutral for the dry streak like follow_failed, written and read again; the cursor moves past it; it counts under its own key in the Play's skipped. Start over takes it back, by prefix beside RETRIED since a list cannot name every handle: the post goes to retry, and the next Play marks it again, or follows and plays it once Kev has listed the author. The log, the Play's history and the Posts CSV say "leads to @b, not on your list" through outcomeWords, on the log line whose link is the post. Start over's button and confirm now name it. Defaults beyond the task: the forwarder's cap check moved below the list read, as a mark costs nothing; the nested Play now takes onePostApi(core, reply, fetchFn) since no replies are handed on, the same reader with less code. Add link and Play links are untouched: resolveLink listing the link's author is Kev's own act of vetting; a waiting link's author was listed when Kev put it in line, and Remove deletes the waiting row with the account, so Play links lists no one new unless the chain now ends elsewhere than when he added it, and then only the author of his own link. Play all only calls playCreator. After this commit the writers of hunter_accounts rows are addAccounts and resolveLink alone (`grep upsert` on hunter_accounts: app/api/admin/route.ts:954, lib/hunter/manual-link.ts:74).
Residual risk: (1) Listing B without Start over on A leaves A's line saying "not on your list" until A is started over: the mark is what was true when it was read. (2) Searching the log for @b does not find the line, whose handle column is A's. (3) A long forward with words of its own in recipe or manual mode stays the forwarder's find, as in DEC-2026-11-02-14. (4) In auto mode a forward whose own words go to the model first pays that one distill on the forwarder, as before: that is the forwarder's own post, not the stranger's.
Evidence: VERIFIED live schema, PostgREST OpenAPI: `handle | string | text | Note: This is a Foreign Key to hunter_accounts.handle`, hunter_posts columns post_id, handle, author_id, likes, outcome, submission_id, read_at: nothing can hold the handle. VERIFIED no CHECK on outcome, insert with handle `zz_probe_no_such_handle_at_all` (`FK target rows for the probe handle: 0`): `probe "queued" -> 23503`, `"follow_failed" -> 23503`, `"retry" -> 23503`, `"rejected" -> 23503`, `"leads_to:probe_b" -> 23503`, `"__invalid__" -> 23503`, `rows landed: 0`. That also closes DEC-15's untested value: 'rejected' passes. Blind spot: an FK-failing insert cannot show a constraint checked later than the FK, and no 23514 was seen on this table to prove the probe can show one; `__invalid__` reaching the FK is what says there is none. VERIFIED Start over's filter on real PostgREST by a read of the same expression: `["outcome.in.(distill_failed,reply_missing,follow_failed,rejected),outcome.like.leads_to:*",38,null]` (DEC-13's 38 marks of aurenvossvt), `["outcome.in.(queued),outcome.like.dist*",69,null]`, so the `in` list and the `like` branch both parse; the write itself was not run live. ### DEC-2026-11-03-16: Filter by NFT reads someone else's public wallet by default: unmoderated pictures, one line turns it off
Context: Kev, 2026-11-03, the filter's spec, his go for this route. GET /api/wallet/nfts only knew the session's wallets. A foreign profile needs that person's NFTs without showing a wallet they linked, which only its owner sees (lib/wallet-nfts). The default the task leaves for Kev to overrule: the filter also works on other people's profiles, so whatever sits in their public wallet, spam airdrops included, can be shown by any signed-in viewer on Enki's own surface.
Options: for the surface: own profile only (no foreign pictures, but the filter is then useless on the profiles Kev described as a "wall"); every profile (chosen, as the task says). For the read: solanaWallets with a flag (one call from reading linked wallets by mistake); a function of its own that cannot reach linked_wallets (chosen). For the bucket: the owner's nfts:list (looking at others would spend the picker's thirty); its own key per user (chosen, as the task says).
Decision: ?creator=<id or handle>, session required. The user is found by id or handle and treated as the profile route treats them (hiddenOwners: banned, deleted or not active answers 404 "Creator not found"; a failed lookup 500 "Creator unavailable"; an unreachable database the outage's 503), then publicSolanaWallet reads the same row the profile route shows, limit(1), never linked_wallets. One index call a list, under nfts:creator, thirty an hour per viewer. Cache-Control and Vary as the own list. An empty ?creator= is a foreign read that finds nobody, never the viewer's own list. Defaults beyond the task: the viewer's own handle goes through the same read and shows only the public wallet, what anyone sees there; a stored address that is no Solana address counts as no wallet and costs no call, as solanaWallets does; the query is unordered as on the profile route so the two cannot name different wallets.

They pass neither the image check nor the 18+ gate (hideAdult reads prompts, a wallet is not a prompt), and a name is the mint's own text. They appear only after a signed-in viewer opens the menu and ticks them, on that viewer's screen; nothing is stored, listed or indexed, and the tile is the Helius CDN's JPEG, so no script and no call to the NFT's host. (4) Each foreign list is one paid index call, 10 Helius credits per lib/wallet-nfts (REPORTED, not seen on a bill), so a viewer can spend at most 30 calls an hour per server instance.

### DEC-2026-11-03-19: Play links lists no one and spends no other creator's mode when a link's chain ends elsewhere now
Context: review of DEC-14 and DEC-15. addLink re-resolves a waiting link through resolveLink, which upserts whatever author the chain ends at now and plays that author in their mode. Two triggers, both reproduced by the review with the real code: the core was deleted after the link went in line, so the forwarder's own words are the core; the status read failed at queue time, so the row sits under the forwarder and the core shows up later. For a moved link whose author is not listed: refuse, leave it waiting (it would stand in line for ever, and Remove takes the whole creator); refuse and mark leads_to:<handle>, as forward() does (chosen, the words and Start over exist). Adding the link again is how a stranger gets listed from here, after which it waits under them. A request without `handle` behaves as before; only the page calls addLink (`grep '"addLink"' app`: app/admin/page.tsx alone).

### DEC-2026-11-03-31: Video posts are saved in hunter_parked, by every address, before a post is marked read
Context: Kev, 2026-11-03: "video posts bitte in einen reiter im admin bereich da speichern bis wir den implementieren die tage. nicht verwerfen, we will implement them, save them." Until now a post with only a video got outcome video_only and lost everything but a count, and a post with both lost its video. XPost.videos was only a number.
Options: storage: a new table (chosen, SQL 64; the tab has text, replies and video data to page over); columns on hunter_posts (a row that vanishes with Remove, and a heavy log read); rows in admin_actions (no paging by kind, no primary key to make a re-read idempotent). What the row holds of a video: FxTwitter's object as it gives it (chosen: every address and whatever else it holds, so the import in a few days picks); a picked subset (the import would be held to my guess). Download now: no, as told. handle: no foreign key (chosen: Remove cascades hunter_posts, and it must not delete what was saved "nicht verwerfen"); a cascade like its neighbour. Replies on a sure post: read them when the reader is free (chosen: Kev's rule that a video in a reply counts, $0); keep today's skip (a video in a reply under a post with a sure prompt would be lost).
Decision: SQL 64, table hunter_parked, primary key post_id, kind 'video' or 'no_media', handle, author_id, url, post_text, replies jsonb [{id, url, text}], videos jsonb (the reader's objects, reply_id when in a reply), photos jsonb (addresses), reach, why, read_at; RLS on, service role only. CreatorDeps' readers keep their shape; postOfFx adds videoData beside the count. In take(), for any mode and door: a free reader reads the author's replies first, once per post (repliesOf); videos are counted on the post and its replies. Any video: an upsert on post_id before anything else, why "no picture" or "beside pictures". No picture on the post or in a reply: outcome video_only, no find. Otherwise the find goes on as before. ### DEC-2026-11-03-59: Approve refuses while the prompt field differs from the row, and the typed words wait
Context: Kev answered yes on 2026-11-03 to DEC-2026-11-03-50's residual risk: a typed edit whose blur save fails stays on screen while the server holds the old prompt, and Approve publishes the old one. Putting the old text back, as takeWhole does, would lose the typing. Reading the case closer: comparing field and row at the click is not enough. The click's own blur sends the save, the row shows the typed words at once, so the two match at the click and only the answer tells; and with the read after a failed save down too, the row stayed on the typed words for good, and a blur could not even send them again.
Options: a compare at the click alone (misses the two above); a compare after the saves through refs filled at render (a failed save's setData is not rendered yet when the next `then` runs); a map of the words whose save failed, read after the saves, plus the compare at the click for words that came from elsewhere (chosen); retry the save inside Approve (more than asked, and a refused save would refuse again).
Decision: impUnsaved, a ref by find. A prompt save that fails stores the words and puts the row back to what it held, so the next blur sends them again; one that goes through removes them; opening the find shows them, also past another find. approveFinds adds the open field if it differs from its row (a read brought other words), waits for the saves, and refuses if any find it was asked for has words waiting: no request, the toast `Nothing was published: the prompt typed for “Vase” is not saved, so click into its field and out again to save it first.`, the field untouched. A blur on words put back to the row's removes them, so Approve is free again. takeWhole removes what saveImpFields stored: it puts the cut back on screen itself, and DEC-50's "Approve publishes what the screen shows" holds.
Defaults beyond the task: (1) A row closed with words waiting refuses too: closed, it shows the old prompt, but the words are the admin's and the sentence says where they are. (2) Approve all refuses the whole press when any of its finds has words waiting, names one, and publishes nothing; the marks are cleared by the press as before, so they are set again. (3) The field in focus when a read brought other words: the click's blur saves the field over them and that is what is published, the screen's words, last writer wins as every field here does.
Residual risk: (1) The words live in the tab: a page reload loses them, with the failed save's toast the only trace. (2) The sentence is a toast of 2.6 s, as every toast on this page; pressing Approve again says it again. (3) A whole text pressed and Approve straight after, that save failing: the cut is published with both toasts in a row, DEC-50's behaviour, not changed here. (4) Words waiting on a find that another admin approved or rejected meanwhile stay in the map until the tab closes, unused.
Evidence: VERIFIED real page in headless Edge, real clicks and keys, the stub keeping the route's edit rules: `PASS  H refused save: Approve publishes nothing  []`, `PASS  H refused save: Approve says so in a sentence`, `PASS  H refused save: the words are still in the field`, `PASS  H in and out of the field saves the words`, `PASS  H then Approve publishes the typed prompt  1`, `PASS  H straight from the field, the save failed: nothing published`, `PASS  H control: straight from the field, saved: publishes the typed prompt  1`, `PASS  H network gone: Approve publishes nothing, and says so`, `PASS  H network back: in and out of the field saves the words`, `PASS  H closed: Approve refuses all the same`, `PASS  H opened again: the words are in the field`, `PASS  H words put back: Approve publishes the prompt on screen`, `PASS  H Approve all with unsaved words in it: nothing published, says so`, `PASS  H a read brought other words: Approve refuses  0`, `PASS  H the field in focus: the click's blur saves it, and the screen's words are published`. `RUN=H,E`: `52 pass, 0 fail`, `console: []`, DEC-50's E checks among them. My first H had `FAIL  H a read brought other words: Approve refuses  1`: the scenario's field was still in focus, so the click's blur saved it and the screen's words went out; the code was right, and that case is now a check of its own. Handler tests with the page's own source: `Tests  55 passed (55)`; the 18 test files that read the page and the Esc scan: `Test Files  18 passed (18)`, `Tests  335 passed (335)`. In-memory mutants: `baseline: 55 passed, 0 failed, 0 not loaded`, Y1 to Y14; Y5 (`ids.includes(impOpen)` dropped) survived, because recording an open field that differs changes nothing for another find's Approve: the condition was dead and it is gone. 13 of 13 others killed; Y13 by the source pin alone, its browser mutant Yb6 by a real check. Browser mutants in the bundle only, Yb1 to Yb9, `survivors: 0 of 1` on the re-run below: first round 8 red at the check named, Yb7 listed SURVIVED because it went red earlier than named, at `FAIL  H straight from the field, the save failed: nothing published`, and the run then threw on the row that was gone; re-run naming that check, `killed Yb7`. Metered calls of one press: none for a saved verdict, none for a refused proof, none before SQL 65. RENEWALS_FIRST_DAY and RENEWALS_PER_DAY in lib/nft-check.ts change it in one line each (a test pins the two numbers, on purpose). (2) A sold NFT stays checkable by the wallet that held it for up to 24 h of a proof's life: the index is not asked again, and all it buys is a verdict on a picture that account could already read. (3) A verdict is per NFT id, not per picture: a mutable NFT that changes its picture keeps its verdict until renewed; the generation routes still judge the real bytes. (4) First checks have no daily limit, only 30 presses a minute per account, in one instance's memory (lib/rate-limit), as the failed ones must stay free; a wallet of 1000 NFTs is up to 1000 judged pictures, 4000 calls at worst. (5) Two tabs: a renewal lost in a race answers 409; a give-back that meets a later claim keeps that renewal spent; a function killed between claim and result loses one renewal. All fail toward fewer judges. (6) A flagged NFT renewed files one case and mail per renewal, at most 7 on its first day, as generate-image files one per request. (7) Past PostgREST's 1000 rows a tile looks grey; its press answers the saved verdict for free. ### DEC-2026-11-04-57: A provider breaker that opens mails OPS_ALERT_EMAILS, one writer per row and at most once an hour per flapping route
Context: Key-theft measures, Kev's go 11-04 ("ffmpeg ja, build"), M1. The breaker opened with console.error only (provider-health.ts reportFailure). Both callers sit in after() (generate-image/route.ts:941, x402/generate/route.ts:645), so the buyer's answer does not wait on the mail. A serverless fleet can fail on many functions at once, and a 429 opens the provider at once while half-open retries every 30 s, so a plain "mail on open" could send about 120 mails an hour.
Options: mail on every open (rejected, the flap above); a new mailed_at column (rejected: an SQL file for one timestamp nobody else reads); an atomic flip plus opened_at as the window (chosen). Within that: the plan had the two provider writes stamp opened_at on every failure (rejected: a sliding window, so a flap that never stops mails once and then never again); stamp only when a mail goes (chosen, so a flap mails once per hour for as long as it lasts).
Decision: movedToOpen() runs update status=down where status<>down returning opened_at; what comes back is the prior value since the flip does not touch it. It tells when any flipped row has opened_at null or at least 1 h old. Provider scope first inserts the route's row (ignoreDuplicates) so a route never seen has something to win. opened_at now means "last told" and survives a close: reportSuccess and runProbe stop nulling it. The mail holds the provider id, the route id or "all routes" and the time, never last_error, because a provider's error can echo what we sent it. A lost mail is not sent again and never fails the caller. An outage that never closes mails once, however long it lasts. Bound under concurrency: one winner per row, at most one extra mail per never-seen route of that provider.
Evidence: VERIFIED `npx vitest run lib/__tests__/provider-health.test.ts`: `Tests 33 passed`, on the real migration in PGlite. Neighbours that run reportFailure (env-01, gemini-refusals, missing-provider-key, x402-settle-route, renderable): `Tests 82 passed`. In-memory mutants, fsModuleCache off, each with MUTANT_APPLIED and a red assertion: first run `killed 15 / 17`, survivors `route: window slides` and `provider: first write overwrites an open row`, each given a test, then `killed 3 / 3` (those two and `no neq`). Others killed include window ignored, window never ends, window off by one, error text in the mail, catch removed, reportSuccess and runProbe nulling opened_at, the flip not scoped. VERIFIED no reader of opened_at outside this file: `grep -rn opened_at lib app` hits only provider-health.ts. REPORTED from this session's plan: live `opened_at not null: */0`. Blind spots: PGlite is one session, so row-lock contention never ran and "one winner" rests on the statement's shape and READ COMMITTED's re-read; no real mail went out (sendMail stubbed); a timeout or thrown adapter never reaches reportFailure (generate-image:929 to the catch-all), so the breaker and this mail cannot see those; no `next build` ran in this checkout, and mailer.ts holds only fetch, so a client bundle reaching provider-health through lib/generation/models.ts gains nothing that breaks (INFERRED, CI's build job decides).
Revert: revert this commit.

The flip fell inside the hour and later failures found the row already down, so a revoked key, the alert this exists for, never mailed. DEC-2026-11-04-57 covered "an outage that never closes mails once", not one that never mails its own opening. A mail Resend refuses: `sendMail ok:false -> warns [] row {"status":"down",...opened_at...}`, then `second open 10 min later, Resend back: mails 0`: the catch was dead code, as in DEC-2026-11-04-73, and its mutant's kill measured a stub that throws. Decision: yoursToTell replaces movedToOpen. It reads the provider's rows. Any row told within the hour: nobody tells, so one provider mails at most hourly however many of its routes flap. Past that, a row in scope is due when never told, or when it answered since its last mail. So an outage mails once, a flap at most hourly, and an outage that begins inside another's hour is told by its first failure past that hour. It stamps by compare-and-set on the value read, so one function wins. sendMail's answer is read: no recipient reached logs and nulls opened_at for that scope, so the next failure tries again; no recipient configured leaves the stamp. The account-wide write still stamps every route, so one outage is one mail across them.

Two functions on two different routes can each win their own row at once, one extra mail. A bound past the hour rests on the failures arriving: no traffic, no reportFailure, no mail. Worst case by arithmetic, all day: 3 providers × 2 recipients × 24 = 144 (INFERRED), only with all three flapping all day. The classifier's words are not changed: `"Your account has been blocked for a policy violation" {"kind":"content"}` means no breaker and no mail, but those strings are the reviewer's wording, not a provider's, and widening it risks one refused prompt taking a provider down for everyone, the risk the classifier's own comment names. ### DEC-2026-11-04-97: Only the timeout tells the breaker, and only when the host had a real window; correction to DEC-2026-11-04-85

### DEC-2026-11-05-03: Step-up tokens say which factor passed; requireAllFactors asks for every enrolled one
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05: "attach wallet muss gefixt werden, sodass man wallet nur mit allen MFAs wechseln darf." requireStepUp takes one token of any factor, so "all" cannot be read from a token today. This commit is the token half; the route and the client follow in the next one.

Decision: mintStepUpToken(userId, scope, factor?), both minting routes pass the factor they checked. requireAllFactors(req, userId, scope, { mandatory }) reads enrolledFactors now, counts a token only with a valid signature, this user, this scope, a jti and a claim enrolled now; tokens are comma separated in X-StepUp-Token; one factor twice counts once by the Map. While any is missing: 401 { stepUp, all, factors, missing }, nothing claimed. wallet-change:<solana address> joins SCOPE and isMoneyScope. The fourth argument mirrors requireStepUp's: without a factor, `mandatory` answers 403 { enroll }, otherwise it proceeds. Nothing else about requireStepUp changes; its single-row claim goes through the same insert.

### DEC-2026-11-05-05: A new wallet signs first, and a change takes every factor
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05: "attach wallet muss gefixt werden, sodass man wallet nur mit allen MFAs wechseln darf", and "ja mail an besitzer". Before this, any password session could add any free address as a primary wallet and re-point itself, and artistPayoutWallet (lib/payments/generation-quote.ts:84) reads that table, so a stolen session could divert an artist's payouts and anyone could pre-claim an address.
Options, where the design left a choice: (1) proof text with the app's name, like the link text (rejected: /api/auth/session accepts any text naming the wallet, the nonce and the app, so the proof would work as a login; the text names no app, and a test sends one to the login route); (2) insert a new row for a removed own address (rejected: VERIFIED live, 1 address has 2 rows only as case variants, `addresses with 2+ rows, exact case: 0`, so an exact-case unique index cannot be ruled out; the removed row comes back by update, one row per address); (3) new row primary from the start (rejected: no read of PostgREST shows indexes, and no migration creates this table; the order works with or without a limit: insert non-primary, re-point, evict, demote, promote, retire); (4) `.neq("token", token)` on the eviction (dropped: a mutant survived, the session has already moved off the old address, so it was dead); (5) a retry after a half-finished switch finishing the job (rejected: it would retire a wallet with no gate).
Decision: As Kev's design: 428 { proof } until each new address signs; the signature checked before the gate, the nonce spent after it; all factors through requireAllFactors, a first wallet too; no factor plus a live wallet of that family 403 { enroll }; no factor and no live wallet of that family passes on the proof. A real switch retires the family's old rows last, drops other sessions on them, mails through lib/security-notice.ts (three an hour per kind; confirmed login email, then a connected Google or X email, then a confirmed email factor, last because a stolen session can plant one). An EVM row never becomes primary, as before: a Solana row stands beside it, and only Solana pays. The client signs with CDP's encodings (signSolanaMessage takes base64 and answers base58, signEvmMessage takes text and answers hex, node_modules/@coinbase/cdp-core/dist/types/types.d.ts:377-390, EIP-191 per @coinbase/cdp-api-client's types); the silent attach stops quietly at any refusal; only ensure({ attached: true }) asks, one factor at a time. lib/ui/kit/serial-asks.ts forgets a scope before its answer settles: it forgot it two microtasks after, so the second factor's ask got the first factor's token back. Found by reading, pinned in serial-asks.test.ts.

### DEC-2026-11-05-13: The side address never stops the money path, and parallel jobs share one attach
Context: Review of 5e01077b..ef7f2a7c. Two client faults on the way to a paid generation. (1) The bridge signed every proof in one Promise.all, so a rejected EVM signature posted nothing and the job failed with CDP's raw error, though the EVM address is informational (DEC-2026-11-05-05: "only Solana pays"). (2) attach had no single flight: parallel jobs reached the same dialog, serial-asks gave them the same token, both posted, one claimed the jti and the other failed with "Every second factor has to confirm this" although the attach landed.
Options for (1): retry the EVM signature (rejected: nothing says it would pass); leave the address out and post again, as the review proposed (chosen). Options for (2): a dialog cache like render-stepup (rejected: requireAllFactors takes a token once, a cache cannot share it); one attach at a time in a ref, as signingIn does (chosen).
Decision: A failed EVM signature sets evmAddress null for that attach and drops its proof, so a new Solana address goes through and a live one only re-points. A failed Solana signature still stops the attach. One attach runs at a time: a silent or an asking call joins an asking one, a silent joins a silent, an asking call waits out a silent one, which stops at the factors, and then goes itself on the session its caller had. A failure reaches every job that shared it; the next call starts anew. Found on the way: the queued call has to re-check the mount after its wait, or a job from the previous account would post on.
Corrections to the bridge test's fake, which hid both faults: it returned an EVM proof entry with no EVM address, accepted a token any number of times, and no test held the silent attach at the point a paid job meets it.
Residual risk, inside the decision: an EVM address that keeps failing to sign stays off the account, silently; nothing asks for it again but the next attach. A silent call joining a silent one has no reachable caller in one mount, so that half of the condition has no test of its own.

Blind spots: CDP is stubbed, so whether real EVM signing fails is not determined (live: 1 of the 2 email accounts with a Solana row has an EVM row, why is not determined, REPORTED by the review); the dialog is a stub; no browser run.

### DEC-2026-11-05-17: A deleted account opens no session by password, wallet, first login, reset code or guardian recovery; correction to docs/specs/SOC-8.md
Context: SOC-8 gap. softDelete keeps password_credentials and user_wallets; only OAuth refused (lib/auth/oauth.ts:482). A deleted account could log in again by password or wallet, and BetaGate admitted the new session. ### DEC-2026-11-05-23: The connect notice tries an unconfirmed login email before the address just connected; correction to DEC-2026-11-05-14
Context: Review finding. A password account has email_verified_at null until an inbox proved it, so securityNoticeAddress skipped its login email. Notices about anything else keep skipping an unconfirmed email. (b) A phisher who first plants a confirmed email factor hears instead of the owner, as the factor comes before the unconfirmed email. (c) Other notices, factor added and wallet attached included, still reach nobody or the factor on such an account; reported to Kev. (d) A reset does nothing for an account with no password credential.

### DEC-2026-11-05-30: A live Solana wallet drops a new EVM address; any live wallet makes a new Solana address ask for a factor; correction to DEC-2026-11-05-05 and -08
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05, "alle ja" on this recommendation. On a factor-free account a stolen session could add its own EVM wallet beside a live Solana wallet on proof alone. That row is a login that outlives the session and a password reset (app/api/auth/session/route.ts maps any live wallet to its account, lib/password-reset.ts removes no wallet row). On an account with a factor the same request asked every factor for a wallet that did not change. Only Solana pays.
Options: ask a factor for a new EVM row on every account (rejected: a factor-free account would then be told to set one up for an address that pays nothing, on a silent attach); drop it when Solana is live (chosen, Kev's rule). For the foreign check on a dropped address: keep the 409 (rejected: a side address would stop the money path, against DEC-2026-11-05-13, for a row nobody writes); do not read it (chosen, one read fewer per re-point). For `evm` in the answer: read back whether the address is live (rejected: one more read on every page load, no client reads the field); the address this request attached, else null (chosen).
Decision: Four cases, as asked. Solana address already a live row: only re-points; the EVM address gets no row, no proof, no signature, no factor, with or without factors. No factor and any live wallet of any family and a new Solana address: 403 { enroll } with the existing sentence, no row. No live wallet and no factor: first attach of both on proof alone, silent. A factor and a new Solana address: every factor, the EVM address going along and replacing the old EVM row. `evm` in the answer names only what this request attached; the session-already-on-it answer no longer repeats what the client sent, which it did without writing anything. No client change: VERIFIED by grep, no file in components, hooks or app reads the field; components/CdpWalletBridge.tsx still sends the address, and its 428 handling only ever sees a Solana entry first now.
Known consequence, as asked: an old account gets no EVM address added later. VERIFIED live read-only GETs, counts only: `live rows 21 accounts with a live row 20 accounts with a factor 0`; `all accounts live solana no evm 19`, of which `origin:wallet ... 17`, `origin:agent ... 1`, `origin:email|cred:true ... 1`; `password-or-social accounts with a live row 2 live solana and no live evm 1 live evm and no live solana 0`. So one account that has an embedded wallet at all stays without an EVM row for good; the other 18 have no embedded wallet. Nobody hits the new 403 today: no account has a live EVM row and no live Solana row.
Corrections, the earlier entries stand as written. DEC-2026-11-05-05 said "no factor and no live wallet of that family passes on the proof" and "a family it has one on" answers enroll: the family no longer matters, any live wallet asks. Its residual (b), the same approval covering any EVM address on a change of EVM alone, no longer exists: there is no change of EVM alone. DEC-2026-11-05-08's "A new row beside a live wallet, with no factor" mail no longer has a case to fire on; the mail stays for an account with factors and for a half-finished switch. Test corrections: the tests that pinned the old rule ("a new EVM address beside a live Solana one needs only its own proof", "switches the EVM family alone") are replaced by tests of the new one, and the bridge's fake lost its newEvmOnly answer, which the real route can no longer give; DEC-2026-11-05-13's point stays pinned by the test that a failed EVM signature leaves the address out of a new Solana attach. "The double attach that lost" now holds a factor: without one it stopped at 403 before reaching what it pins.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) A wallet that fails its EVM signature on a first attach stays without an EVM row for good, as nothing adds one later. (b) A small race on a first attach: if another tab wrote the EVM row between this request's two ownership reads, its Solana read having come first, this request has a fresh Solana address and a live EVM row, and answers 403 enroll; the silent attach stops quietly and the next one re-points. Excusing a live EVM row the request names is what would open the hole: any stolen session can name a public address (mutant 1.9). (c) A session can still plant a first wallet on an account with none, Kev's rule 3, DEC-2026-11-05-05 (d).
Evidence: VERIFIED tests `Tests  140 passed (140)` in the gate, ownership, bridge and ban files. In-memory mutants, baseline `Tests  73 passed (73)`, fsModuleCache off: `ALL 9 KILLED` (dropping the break, the old family rule, always mandatory, three answers, three on the row of an address being attached). ### DEC-2026-11-05-31: A wallet switch waits out the newest factor's first 24 hours
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05, on the proposal in DEC-2026-11-05-12: after a new factor a wallet change only goes through after 24 hours. Without it, a stolen session on a factor-free account plants a factor and moves the wallet seconds after the mail.
Options: read the wait inside requireAllFactors (rejected: every scope would pay for a rule only this one has); a helper beside enrolledFactors called by the route (chosen, as asked); one shared read for both (rejected: enrolledFactors keeps its head count, and the other callers do not want the dates).
Decision: newFactorWaitUntil in lib/mfa.ts, one constant NEW_FACTOR_WAIT_MS. Only when retired rows exist: 403 { wait: true, until, error } with a plain sentence naming the time. After the signature and before requireAllFactors, so no token or nonce goes on a refusal. "That counts" is enrolledFactors' set: an email factor on a password account starts no wait, on a no-password account it does. A pending factor starts none. A failed read of any of the three tables is 503. A date that does not parse goes the same way, through a RangeError on purpose, no branch of its own. No account without a factor is touched: that stays the enroll answer.
Client, read and tested, no change: `if (!reply.res.ok) throw new Error(reply.answer.error || ...)` surfaces the sentence on the way to a paid generation; the silent attach's `.catch` stays quiet, as with enroll. Both pinned in lib/__tests__/cdp-wallet-bridge.test.ts.
The race, kept: the helper and requireAllFactors each read the factors, so a factor landing between the two reads is not seen by the wait. It is acceptable: the factor gate after it then asks for that factor too, and a token for it can only be minted after it is enrolled, so a request that already holds one started after the factor existed and its wait read saw it. INFERRED from lib/webauthn.ts's verifyStepUpToken and enrolledFactors, not staged as a test. A window of a few milliseconds and no way to use it.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) The wait reads retired rows, as asked. An account with a young factor and only a live EVM row can still add a Solana wallet with every factor and no wait: nothing is retired. VERIFIED live, count only: `live evm and no live solana 0`. (b) A person who enrolls their first factor because of the enroll answer, then moves their own wallet, waits a day. That is the rule. (c) Removing the new factor ends the wait if an older one remains, and it takes every factor since DEC-2026-11-05-11, the owner's older one too. Where the planted factor is the only one, removing it leaves the enroll answer: nothing moves either way. (d) No state on the account says a wait is running; the sentence appears only when someone tries.
Evidence: VERIFIED whole suite on this tree only with the suite's temp folder on D:, as C: has 0.26 GB free and lib/video/__tests__/transcode.test.ts writes up to 300 MB (first run: `ENOSPC: no space left on device`, a machine fault, reported to Kev; the second run green). VERIFIED live read-only GETs: `mfa_factors.confirmed_at all 200 */0`, `webauthn_credentials.created_at all 200 */0`, so both columns exist and both tables are empty today (`accounts with a factor 0`): no account is held now, and the live data cannot show a real row's date format. migrations/2026-07-11-webauthn.sql:14 declares created_at NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), migrations/2026-10-07-mfa-factors.sql:24 confirmed_at nullable. VERIFIED tests: 14 new in wallet-change-gate.test.ts, 2 in the bridge file. In-memory mutants, baseline green, fsModuleCache off: `ALL 20 KILLED` on the route and the helper, 2 / 2 on the client; one survived first (the silent attach asking on any 403 only posts once more), the silent test now counts the posts. ### DEC-2026-11-05-32: A guardian-approved deletion waits out a ban; the delete dialog names the embedded wallet
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05: "alle ja". A banned account's funds door is /banned, and softDelete takes the session that opens it. The delete dialog said nothing about the wallet of an account that has one. A door for deleted accounts, a balance check and emailing anything about keys are not in this: Kev is still deciding those.
Options: for the hold, refuse the guardian's approve (rejected: approve only records, and a ban lifted within the week should still finish); check in softDelete (rejected: it has no way to answer, and the POST path never gets there banned); check at the one call that finalises on approval (chosen). For the sentence: a new request for the wallet (rejected, as asked); cdpRuntimeExpected() from lib/cdp-bridge.ts, which PaymentPanel already reads (chosen).
Decision: GET /api/account/delete reads activeBanFor before softDelete, once approvals reach the threshold on a request not expired. A running ban answers 200 { status: "held", message, approved, threshold }: nothing deleted, request stays pending, no cookie touched, and the next poll finishes it if the ban was lifted. A failed read answers 503 and deletes nothing; the dialog keeps polling. The dialog's waiting view shows the server's sentence and the title "Deletion on hold", and goes back when no longer held. "Every path" checked by reading: app/api/account/delete/approve/route.ts only writes approved_at and never finalises, pinned by a test; POST's no-guardian softDelete cannot be reached by a banned session, as resolveSessionUserId answers null and the route 401, pinned by a test; a failed ban read there throws before the delete (lib/session-user.ts unread). `grep softDelete` has 3 hits, the definition and these two.
The sentence "Move your funds or export your key first: after deletion you can no longer reach this wallet." sits in the confirm view behind cdpRuntimeExpected(): true for an email, Google or X login with CDP configured (providers/index.tsx:24), false for a wallet login.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) A wallet-origin account signed in through Google or X has a runtime and no embedded wallet (/api/auth/wallet/jwt answers walletAccount), so it reads the sentence too, though wrong only in "this wallet". ### DEC-2026-11-05-41: Recovery codes: one code and a session remove one named factor; what Kev decided with no code
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05: "was is mit wiederherstellungs codes, fix that", and on the lost-factor design "build", "gehe dann das sicherste an"; "support weg". A factor is removed only with every factor (DEC-2026-11-05-11), so someone who lost their only factor cannot open their wallet (403 locked), someone who lost one of two cannot change any factor or wallet, and a factor planted by a stolen session outlives a reset (DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 4). The design was decided in the brief; this entry logs what the code had to add to it.
Options: per-instance limiter for attempts (rejected in the brief: lib/rate-limit is per instance); a lock written after the compare, as lib/mfa.ts checkCode does (rejected, see below); a code as a step-up factor (rejected in the brief: a code removes a factor and does nothing else).
Decision: as designed. Ten codes of 16 Crockford base32 characters (80 bits, crypto.randomInt), shown as XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX, stored only as an HMAC-SHA256 under an AUTH_PEPPER-derived key with its own info string, over userId:code. Issued at a factor's confirm or registration when the account holds no unused code, new set behind requireAllFactors with mandatory true and its own scope recovery-codes, new rows first. POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery/redeem takes a session and a code for a factor enrolledFactors returns.
What I added or chose, for Kev to challenge:
(1) The fifth try's claim writes the lock itself, where lib/mfa.ts writes the count and locks in a second update. In checkCode a failure between the two leaves failed_attempts at 5 with no lock, and that branch answers "locked" forever. Here that would close the one way out. The same MAX_ATTEMPTS and doubling; a right code on the last try passes and clears it. So during that last try's compare, parallel requests read as locked. lib/mfa.ts is not changed here; the stuck state stays possible there, INFERRED by reading, not staged.
(2) Confirming a factor that already counts issues no codes. checkCode answers "ok" with confirm: true on a confirmed factor too, and that route takes one factor. Without this check, on an account with no unused code one factor would get itself a set, and a code removes the other factor: "every factor" worth one. The route reads enrolledFactors before checkCode. A second, new factor on an account with no unused code does issue: its setup took every factor.
(3) The addresses are read before the attempt is claimed. A failed read answers 500 with nothing spent, so nobody loses a factor unheard because of an outage. Beyond the brief, which only said to mail.
(4) Input also reads O as 0 and I and L as 1, as Crockford's alphabet is made for: these codes get written on paper, and each misread character costs an attempt. Beyond the brief's "case, dashes and spaces".
(5) The SQL writes GRANT ... TO service_role, beside the REVOKE as in 2-mfa-factors.sql: SQL 64, 69 and 72 write theirs out, as Supabase announced an end to default grants on new tables. Without it the routes could read 42501 on a new project. Also a partial unique index on cancel_token_hash, for the mail link's lookup with no session.
(6) No head reads on the new tables: postgrest-js answers a missing table's empty 404 with no error and no count (test double, lib/__tests__/_fake-postgrest.ts), which would read as zero codes. So the count selects the ids.
(7) Every new route resolves through resolveSessionUserWithBan, as the step-up routes do: a banned account can use a code, as its money sits behind that factor.
Kev's decisions with no code, 2026-11-05, recorded here as asked. (a) "ja np wg session, man kann ja eh keinen unfug machen solange mfa aktiviert ist, man ist ja auch bei X angemeldet zb": no sign-out control is built; this answers DEC-2026-11-05-34 residual (a). His sentence holds only for what a factor gates: DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 1 (disconnecting Google or X asks no factor and sends no mail) is an exception, still open, and is not built here. (b) "wallet wechsel ist erstmal raus": the own wallet stays parked. (c) The funds door and any way of sending a key are off: a key cannot be sent at all, as Coinbase's iframe holds it (components/settings/KeyExport.tsx). (d) "key echtes löschen = löschen von allen daten mit kritischer abfrage, aber login geht ja dennoch" stays out of scope here.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) On an account whose only factor is the one removed, the code does open the wallet in effect: with no factor the session alone passes wallet/jwt, as for any factor-free account. That is the way out it was built for, and a stolen session holding a code gets it too; the mail goes at once. On two factors the other still locks the wallet, tested. (b) Whoever plants the first factor is shown the first codes. They work only with a signed-in session, so a reset that ends that session ends them for practical use, but they stay valid until a new set. ### DEC-2026-11-05-42: No code left: a mailed code starts a 5 day wait the owner can cancel; correction to what Kev was told
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05, on the lost-factor design: "build", "gehe dann das sicherste an". Someone who lost the paper too needs a way out with no staff, and a stolen session holding an inbox must not get one quietly. The design was decided in the brief: POST /request sends a 6 digit code, POST /request/confirm starts the wait, DELETE /request or the mail link cancels it, POST /request/finish removes the factor, attach-wallet holds during the wait.
Options: for the cancel, a remaining factor only, as Kev was told (rejected, see 1); for the start, write the wait and then mail, undoing it when no mail went (rejected, see 2); for a dead request, a cron (out of scope; treated as closed on read).
Decision: as designed. What I added or chose, for Kev to challenge:
(1) Correction to what Kev was told: he was told "a remaining factor" cancels. Any one factor cancels, the one named as lost included. Holding it proves it is not lost, and that is the protection against a hijacked inbox naming a factor the owner still has. An account with one factor could not cancel at all otherwise. Residual, inside the decision: a stolen session holding a planted factor can cancel the owner's request until that session ends. A password reset ends it; a passwordless account's session runs its 30 days. Kev 2026-11-05 accepted session theft as a topic: "ja np wg session".
(2) The start is three steps: the code is spent, so of two requests carrying it one goes on; the start mail goes out; then the wait starts. With the wait written first, a crash between the two leaves a wait running that nobody heard of, which is the one thing the design must not do. This order's failure is on the safe side: a crash after the mail leaves a mail saying a wait started with no wait running. Not one mail delivered: the code comes back, no wait, 502.
(3) An email factor named as the lost one does not count as the confirmed address. Whoever reads that inbox holds the factor, and whoever does not could never get the code; so that account hears "only a recovery code helps" instead of waiting on a mail that cannot arrive.
(4) Adding a factor closes a request naming that kind. "Treated as closed on read" alone would let a request for a removed authenticator come back to life when a new one is set up, and remove the new one at finish. One write in codesForNewFactor, which both factor routes already call. A removal by code closes it in the same update; the two DELETE routes rely on the read, as a passkey's DELETE may not be the last one.
(5) The address list is read before finish claims the request. A failed read answers 500 with nothing removed. A cancel is the other way round: it stands whether or not its mail goes, since it can only make the account safer.
(6) POST /request and POST /request/confirm share the one attempt counter recovery codes use. A pending code is no request: the banner, the hold and GET show a request only from confirm on.
(7) A closed request keeps code_sent_at and the day's count, so a cancel buys no extra code.
(8) The link uses appUrl() from lib/auth/oauth.ts, as the brief says, with the guardian link's ?token= form. The guardian link itself reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_ORIGIN (app/api/recovery/guardians/route.ts:107). appUrl's last fallback is localhost:3008, so production depends on OAUTH_APP_URL or NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL being set, which the wallet JWT's issuer and the OAuth redirect already need (.env.example:7). The production value was not read here.
(9) No cron exists for this and none is added, so correction to "mail at start and end" as Kev was told it: the end mail goes out at finish, not when the 5 days are over. A wait that ends and is not finished closes after 7 days with no mail.
(10) The banner takes the 30 px slot with no X, as it is the owner's in-app warning. The 2FA bar and a trial line keep the slot, as with the guardian warning; Settings shows its own strip either way, unless the shell's is up. Once the date passed it says "A factor recovery can finish now", beyond the sentence in the brief, as a request that can finish is the riskier state.
The confirmed address, read live (VERIFIED, read-only, counts and status only): `users email columns 206 0-0/46`, `users both set 200 0-0/1` (email_ct and email_verified_at, one row, as written by lib/auth/oauth.ts emailColumns for a new Google login), `creds all 206 0-0/3`, `creds verified 200 0-0/1`, `identities google 200 0-0/1`, `identities x 200 */0`. So the order in the brief works as written: password_credentials.email with email_verified_at, then users.email_ct with email_verified_at, then a confirmed email factor. At most 2 of the 46 accounts have a confirmed address today, and the others can only use a code. A wallet account that connected Google later has an auth_identities email and nothing on users, so it counts as no confirmed address: the column does not say the provider vouched for it.
What these mails mean for DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 2: all four recovery mails (a code used, wait started, wait cancelled, factor removed at finish) go to every address, deduplicated ignoring case: the login email even if unconfirmed, every auth_identities email, the users email, a confirmed email factor. They pass no limiter, so the start of a wait is never dropped. Every other notice keeps the one-address order of securityNoticeAddress, so point 2 stays open for those: an attacker's connected Google still outranks an unconfirmed login email on the factor, wallet, withdrawal and export notices. The 6 digit code mail is the only one that goes to the one confirmed address, as a code in every inbox would widen who can start a wait.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) Every address gets the cancel link, so a stranger at a mistyped login email, or an attacker who connected their own Google, can cancel a request and learns the account exists and which factor it names. They can only stop a removal, and every address hears that too. (b) Session plus inbox: the wait runs and the owner has 5 days and every address to stop it. An owner who reads none of them loses the factor. That is the design. (c) DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 1 is still open: a stolen session can disconnect Google with no factor and no mail, which removes that address from this list too. users.email_ct stays. (d) A request can be started again right after a cancel, up to five codes a day; each start mails everyone, and nothing blocks it. (e) During the wait only a wallet change is held. Every other gate still asks its factors. (f) The hold reads the row, then enrolledFactors; a factor removed between them is a few milliseconds of a stale hold, on the safe side. (g) The banner reads once per session, module-cached, so a request started on another device shows after the next load; the mail goes at once. (h) The token sits in the link's query string, so it can reach an access log; all it can do is cancel. (i) Someone whose only factor is lost stays locked out of the wallet for those 5 days, unless they hold a code.
Evidence: VERIFIED live, read-only: the counts above, and `mfa_recovery (expected absent) 404 PGRST205`. VERIFIED tests through the real routes and the real session lookup with a captured mail, `Tests  235 passed (235)` over lib/__tests__/mfa-recovery-request.test.ts, mfa-recovery-codes.test.ts and wallet-change-gate.test.ts. In-memory mutants, baseline green, fsModuleCache off: `killed 115 / 115`; a first run left five alive, each one a real gap: two requests past the attempt claim (the race is now staged, one held at its update while the other finishes), two cancels at once, a right code clearing the attempts, and one mutant whose anchor matched twice, which is no kill. A sixth showed a check that could never fire, row.ready_at beside code_hash, and that check is gone. The whole suite count is in the commit message. Blind spots: a fake PostgREST, so PostgREST's own encoding of the conditional updates and of the timestamps is not exercised, and "two at once" stages the race the fake can stage, with no real lock contention; the clock is the server's, so the wait's boundaries were tested one second either side, not across a time zone; no mail was sent or read in an inbox; the cancel page's GET was shown to do nothing by reading it (no effect, one fetch, on the button) and by the route having no GET, not by a mail scanner; the Settings area and the banner are pinned as source text, as the agents' browser pane stops at the access gate.
Revert: revert this commit.

### DEC-2026-11-05-45: A first factor gets its own recovery codes; a new set tells the owner and cannot leave zero; a further passkey stops a request out loud; corrections to DEC-2026-11-05-41 and -42
Context: A review of 7a0c4ceb..ed99b909. Reproduced first, at ed99b909, through the real routes: a stolen session plants a first factor and keeps its ten codes, the planted factor goes, the owner adds his own passkey and is issued none, Settings says "10 left", and any session holding a kept code strips his passkey and opens the wallet: `owner's first passkey answers { verified: true }`, `Settings tells the owner { available: true, codesLeft: 10, request: null }`, `strip 200`, `wallet jwt with the stale stolen session 200`. The same run: a second passkey closed a running request with no cancel mail (`request after second passkey { factor: null, ready_at: null, token: null }`), a new set sent no mail (`mails after a new set 0`), and two new sets at once left no working code (`two new sets at once 200 200 unused rows left 0`).
Options: for the first factor, keep the brief's "when the account holds no unused code" (rejected: that is the hole); delete the unused codes at every removal (rejected: a code's own removal must leave the others working, DEC-2026-11-05-41); issue a new set when the factor is the account's first (chosen, the review's fix). For two new sets, a created_at cut (rejected: the server's clock against the database's); the rows read before the insert (chosen, no clock). For the notice, in the route (rejected: the first factor's set kills codes too); in newCodeSet (chosen).
Decision: (1) codesForNewFactor takes the factors from before the new one. None before it: newCodeSet, whatever the table holds. A further factor with unused codes still issues nothing. The passkey route now reads them before its insert; a failed read leaves the passkey standing with no codes in the answer, as a failed write does. (2) newCodeSet reads the older rows, inserts the new ten, then deletes only what it read. So two at once leave the set of whichever read last. (3) When unused codes die, every address hears, through mailEach, with no code in the text. This is narrower than the review's "one mail after every new set": a set over none, or over used ones, kills nothing the owner holds, and it would double the factor-added mail on every first factor. Mine, for Kev to challenge. (4) A request still running when its factor is added to (only a further passkey reaches this) closes through closeAndTell, so every address hears the stop. A pending code, a request past its seven days and a request whose factor was already gone close in silence, as nothing that ran was stopped.

It takes every factor twice, in two tabs. (d) Finishing a recovery with another factor left keeps the unused codes and the panel still counts them: open for Kev, see the entry for what stays with him. The finding's case, a finish that leaves no factor, is closed by (1) and tested. (e) A planter who holds every factor can still make a set over none, unheard: nothing the owner holds dies, and the factor-added mail told him earlier.

### DEC-2026-11-05-46: A planted email factor gets no cancel link; a start that did not land does not say started; a 502 changes nothing; a broken factor row closes no way out; corrections to DEC-2026-11-05-41 and -42
Context: A review of 7a0c4ceb..ed99b909. Reproduced first, at ed99b909, through the real routes: a stolen session plants an email factor, its session ends, and the attacker's mailbox cancels the owner's request again and again with no session at all: `round 1 start mail to [ 'owner@gmail.test', 'attacker@evil.test' ]` and the same for rounds 2 and 3, each cancel 200, then `owner's wallet after three rounds 403`. Also confirmed by reading lib/mfa-recovery.ts: the start write had no select, so a parallel request for another factor answered 200 started with no wait; a right code in a mail outage cleared the lock ladder though the brief says "502, state unchanged"; lib/mfa.ts confirmedEmailFactor threw on a row that does not open, which turned every redeem and finish into 500 and every confirm into 502 for that account; and the open cancel route had no limiter, though proxy.ts:45-47 says its neighbours are limited.
Options: for the link, never mail it to any email factor (rejected: an owner with a real email factor and a lost authenticator would lose his link for nothing, and the review's narrower fix closes the case); no mail at all to that address (rejected: the brief says every address hears, and that address may be the owner's); no link to the address of the factor named in the request (chosen). For a 502, move the clear only (rejected: the claim's count stays, and a right code on the last try would leave a lock); move the clear and restore what the claim wrote (chosen). For the broken row, catch in everyAddress (rejected: confirmedAddress reads the same thing and fails the same way); catch in confirmedEmailFactor around the decrypt only (chosen, as usersEmail does).
Decision: (1) When the request names the email factor, its own address gets the start mail with no link and no token, and the sentence "open Settings, Recovery, Lost a factor, and cancel it with this email code". Every other address gets the link. The match ignores case. Both mails count as delivered. It can still cancel by step-up, with a session. (2) The start write reads back its row. None came back: no wait runs and the answer is the plain 404, "No code is waiting. Ask for a new one." (3) ATTEMPTS_CLEARED moves to the start write, and a 502 restores the attempts as read, beside the code. An outage costs a right code nothing. Parallel wrong guesses during that mail are given back with it, which takes holding the right code to reach. (4) confirmedEmailFactor answers null for a row that does not open and still throws on a failed read. Also changes securityNoticeAddress: such a row used to drop that notice, now it goes to the next address. (5) POST /request/cancel takes the guardians' per-instance limiter, 10 a minute per network, before the token lookup.
Corrections, the earlier entries stand as written: DEC-2026-11-05-42 residual (a) said those who get the link "can only stop a removal" and named a stranger or a connected Google. For a planted email factor that stop was the whole way out, for as long as it liked, with no session, which the residual in its point 1 said ends with the session. DEC-2026-11-05-42 point 2 named only the crash case for "says a wait started with no wait running"; a parallel request reached it too, and now it answers so. DEC-2026-11-05-41 point 3 said a failed read refuses, and did not name a broken row.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) A request naming another factor still mails an email factor's address the link, as the review said: an attacker holding both a planted authenticator and a planted email factor can cancel the authenticator's request, so the owner removes the email factor first. The Lost a factor area says so; see the entry for the area. (b) If the factor's address is also the owner's login or Google address, the owner gets no link either; he reads that inbox, so he holds the factor and cancels by step-up. With no session he cannot: same as a request he did not start. (c) In the parallel case every address has already been told of a wait that does not run, with a dead link. The safe side, as nothing can be removed. (d) The limiter is per instance and per network, like its neighbours: it keeps a loop off the database, and no token can be guessed either way. (e) A stolen session holding a planted factor can still cancel by step-up until it ends: DEC-2026-11-05-42 point 1.
Evidence: VERIFIED new tests through the real routes with a captured mail, `Tests  175 passed (175)` over lib/__tests__/mfa-recovery-request.test.ts and mfa-recovery-codes.test.ts. The factor row that does not open is real garbage through the real decrypt. The race is staged by holding the start write while the factor changes, the fake's hold, with no real lock contention. In-memory mutants, baseline `Tests  175 passed (175)`, fsModuleCache off: `killed 18 / 18`; a first run left one alive, the token in the linkless mail, and that test now compares the owner's token. Blind spots: a fake PostgREST; no mail was sent or read in an inbox; a real mail client's preview of the linkless text was not seen; how often a factor row does not open was not measured: REPORTED from DEC-2026-11-05-41, `factors all 200 */0`, so no live account has one today. The whole suite count is in the commit message.

### DEC-2026-11-05-49: A hijacked inbox alone takes a factor away on a password account: open for Kev; what else stays with him; corrections to DEC-2026-11-05-41, -42 and -48
Context: A review of 7a0c4ceb..ed99b909. Most findings were fixed in DEC-2026-11-05-45 to -48. These move the decided design or need his word, or are records that were wrong. SQL 74's header and its README row are the only files changed here.
Options: build the review's recommendation for (1) (rejected: it touches the decided design, it takes the way out from a password user who lost the paper, and the task says a decision only Kev can make is reported, not fixed); say nothing until he answers (rejected: DEC-2026-11-05-42 reads as safer than it is).
Decision: Nothing built for (1), (2) and (3). Open for Kev, each with its smallest fix, recommendation first:
(1) CRITICAL. An inbox alone removes a factor on a password account and opens the wallet. DEC-2026-11-05-42 point 1 called the any-factor cancel "the protection against a hijacked inbox", and its residual (b) said "the owner has 5 days and every address to stop it". Neither holds for the inbox that resets the password. lib/password-reset.ts signs the owner out everywhere and deletes every auth_identities row, with no mail to them, and hands the attacker a fresh session. So the start mail goes to the login inbox alone, the attacker deletes it, the owner has no session to step up with and no link, and after 5 days the factor goes. Before this build the same attacker stayed at 403 locked forever. It breaks Kev's rule at lib/mfa.ts:70-74, that an inbox which resets the password is no second factor. Recommended: on a password account the mail path refuses when the login inbox is the only address the request would reach, and for 5 days after an inbox reset, so only a code helps; and the reset mails every address before it deletes the identities. Cost: a password user with no other address who lost the paper has no way out, which is the state before this build. The other answer: accept it, and say plainly that on a password account a factor is only a 5 day delay against a hijacked inbox.
(2) An account with no confirmed address, an X account for example, has no way out of a planted factor. DEC-2026-11-05-42 said "the others can only use a code" and did not name that a planter holds those codes. The wallet stays 403 with no path and no staff. Smallest closure: ask an X account for a confirmed address before it can add a first factor, so a planter meets the same mail path as everyone else.
(3) Finishing a recovery with another factor left keeps the unused codes, and the panel counts them, though that person walked this path because the paper is gone. A found paper plus a session can strip the factor that is left. One line in finishRemoval deletes them. The review called it his, as it goes beyond the design. The case it was written for, a finish that leaves no factor, is closed by DEC-2026-11-05-45.
Added to the residuals, no code, as the review asked: (4) Session plus inbox can keep the wallet held with no gap, by cancelling through the link and starting again, up to five codes a day, each mailing every address. DEC-2026-11-05-42 residual (d) named the restart and the mails, not the hold. Nothing moves, and wallet change is parked (Kev: "wallet wechsel ist erstmal raus"). (5) A stolen session alone also keeps the owner out of the mail path: five asks a day use up the send cap, a new code replaces the one he is about to type, and five wrong confirms lock both confirm and redeem, up to a day a round. DEC-2026-11-05-41 residual (c) named only redeem's counter. On a passwordless account this runs the session's 30 days. Kev accepted session theft as a topic, "ja np wg session", and the owner cannot be harmed further by it.
Corrections, the earlier entries stand as written: (a) DEC-2026-11-05-42 gave a false reason for not counting a connected Google address: "the column does not say the provider vouched for it". auth_identities.email_verified says exactly that, lib/auth/oauth.ts:382 writes it. The code rightly follows the brief's order. The true reason: a session under ten minutes old on a factor-free account can link any Google account (app/api/auth/oauth/[provider]/start/route.ts:60), so an identity row proves nothing about the owner. I had read the users table for that sentence and not this one. (b) SQL 74's header and README row said "any time, before or after the deploy". Deployed first, the factor mails and the step-up dialog name an area that is hidden until it runs, so both now say before the deploy. No statement changed. (c) DEC-2026-11-05-48 and commit 15197fca give the mutants' baseline as `Tests  275 passed (275)`. The run printed `Tests  274 passed (274)`: I wrote the number from memory after adding an assertion, not a test. The kills stand.
Rejected, no code: the finding that "Lost this factor?" can open Settings under the sheet that asked. Not reproduced. The z values are as it says, sheet 10000 against the panel's 160, but none of the eight files that render a BottomSheet calls guarded, withStepUp, useStepUp or a signing call (grep, 0 hits each), and the one component with an alert dialog and a step-up, PromptEditor, closes it on the action. So no path that asks from inside a sheet was found. The dialog's comment names the z order, not a flow. Whatever is open can be closed by hand and Settings is then there, so the failure would be small. Not driven on a phone, which is the check it asked for.
