### DEC-2026-11-05-50: One inbox that signs in by itself cannot start or finish the mail path; a password reset tells every address it had; closes DEC-2026-11-05-49 point 1
Context: Kev, 2026-11-05 evening, answering DEC-2026-11-05-49's recommendations: "fix the offene sachen". His rule at lib/mfa.ts:70-74 (2026-10-07): an inbox that can reset the password is no second factor. DEC-2026-11-05-49 point 1 (VERIFIED probe there): a hijacked login inbox resets the password, lib/password-reset.ts signs the owner out everywhere and deletes every auth_identities row with no mail, the reset's session starts the mail path, the start mail reaches that inbox alone and is deleted, and after 5 days the factor is gone and the wallet JWT answers 200.
Options: a password account only (rejected for the Google case, DEC-2026-11-05-51); a 5 day refusal after every reset (not needed, DEC-2026-11-05-52); count the address list, as decided (chosen).
Decision: lib/security-notice.ts addressList answers everyAddress and oneDoor: the list holds one distinct address, ignoring case, and that address is a door (the login email, a connected Google or X account's, the email on users). A confirmed email factor's address is no door unless one of those shares it: it opens no session. requestRemoval refuses after no_address and before any code is written; confirmRemoval asks again before the attempt is claimed; finishRemoval asks again before the claim. All three answer 409 with ONE_DOOR: "Your only email address can also sign you in, so it cannot prove it is you. Use a recovery code." GET /api/auth/mfa/recovery carries that sentence as mailRefused (null otherwise), and Settings shows it where No code left was; a recovery code still works there. completePasswordReset reads everyAddress once the password changed and before the connected logins go, and after the evictions mails each address (mailEach): the time, that every device was signed out and the Google or X logins removed, and if it was not them: "someone reset it with a code sent to your login email, or with your guardians' approval. Secure that email account first, then reset your password again: that signs them out." No "contact Enki". A failed read or a failed mail never undoes the reset.
What I chose, for Kev to challenge: (1) In confirm the check comes before the attempt claim, so no try is spent on a refusal. A failed address read there now answers 500 with nothing spent; before it was a 502 after the claim. One existing test's expected status moved for that reason, and it now also asserts failed_attempts 0. (2) The reset reads the addresses after the password update: a read before it would mail for a reset that then failed, and a failed read must not stop a reset. Cost: an outage at that one read means nobody hears of that reset; it is logged. (3) A refusal at confirm or finish leaves the pending code or the request as it is: it can go on once a second address is back, or runs out as any other. (4) The request tests' fixture now gives a password account a connected Google, as the login alone is refused; the tests that counted one mail now name both addresses.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) Accepted with Kev's go on the recommendation: a password user whose only address is the login email, with no code left, has no way out of a lost factor, the state before DEC-2026-11-05-42. (b) Open for Kev, not built: on an account whose one door is a Google address and whose factor is an email factor at another address, that door's holder can name the email factor. The list holds two addresses, so the path runs, and the factor's own address hears with no link (DEC-2026-11-05-46 point 1): it can stop the removal only with a session, which a hijacked Google login may have taken from him. Not counting the named email factor's address would close it, and would also take away the owner's way out of a planted email factor (lib/__tests__/mfa-recovery-request.test.ts "a planted one cannot stop the owner with no session, so its removal finishes"). The same trade DEC-2026-11-05-46 made, now in the open. (c) Two addresses means the owner hears, not that he reads: an owner who reads neither for 5 days loses the factor, as DEC-2026-11-05-42 residual (b) said. (d) The reset mail also goes to the login inbox, whose reader may be the one who reset it; the other addresses are why it exists. (e) The status read now reads the address list too, 4 more reads per GET /api/auth/mfa/recovery (INFERRED from the code, not timed); a failed one fails that GET as the other three reads do.
Evidence: VERIFIED tests through the real routes and the real session lookup with a captured mail, new file lib/__tests__/inbox-door.test.ts and the Settings render in mfa-recovery-dialog.test.ts: `Tests  126 passed (126)` over inbox-door, mfa-recovery-request and mfa-recovery-dialog. DEC-2026-11-05-49's probe 1 runs there through the real forgot and reset-code routes: the reset mails [owner-login, owner-second] before the Google row goes, the reset's session asks and gets 409 with ONE_DOOR, no mail goes, the wallet JWT stays 403 and the passkey stays. Another account's rows stand first in users, password_credentials, auth_identities, mfa_factors, mfa_recovery and auth_sessions, and afterEach asserts them unchanged and unmailed. In-memory mutants, baseline `Tests  126 passed (126)`, fsModuleCache off: `killed 22 / 23` in the first run; the one left did not load (my move put the read inside the mail call), which is no kill; fixed to land after the identity delete, `killed 1 / 1`. So 23 of 23: the door rule's four ways of being wrong, each check removed or moved behind the claim or the send, each route's answer, the status, the reset's read order, recipients, a failed read or mail undoing the reset, the time and the advice, and Settings with and without the sentence. The whole suite count is in the commit message. Blind spots: a fake PostgREST; no mail was sent; Settings was driven as a function call, not in a browser, as the agents' pane stops at the access gate; for about a second the served lib/password-reset.ts named everyAddress before its import line was in (my edit order, against docs/change_management.md rule 1: a ReferenceError only for a reset that ran in that second; not checked in the dev server log).
Revert: revert this commit (DEC-2026-11-05-51 and -52 go with it).

### DEC-2026-11-05-52: No 5 day hold after a reset: no session without a factor can bring the list down to one door after it, and no other inbox alone opens a session on an account; SQL 74 unchanged
Context: The brief's (1d) and (1e): verify whether, after an inbox reset and with no factor in hand, that session can bring everyAddress down to a single door; if so, also refuse the mail path for 5 days after a reset. Verify there is no other inbox-only door.
Options: a stamp and a 5 day refusal after every reset (rejected: no path found that it would close, and it would cost an owner who reset his own password 5 days of no mail path); none (chosen).
Decision: none built. What can change the list, read in the code at this commit: password_credentials is updated in three places and none writes email (app/api/auth/password/first-login/route.ts:68, lib/access-invite.ts:97, lib/password-reset.ts:36; register only inserts a new account and answers 409 on an existing email, register/route.ts:70). users.email_ct is written only by emailColumns (lib/auth/oauth.ts:330), called only from createUser for a new Google account (:447). auth_identities rows go in account deletion (behind requireStepUp "delete-account", app/api/account/delete/route.ts:74), the disconnect (every factor from the next commit), the reset itself, and the OAuth callback's undo of the row that same call inserted; a link needs requireAddFactor (oauth start/route.ts:60), which with a factor is every factor (lib/webauthn.ts:208). An email factor goes only with every factor (app/api/auth/mfa/[kind]/route.ts:70), a code, or the path itself. So after the reset, which already removed every identity, nothing without a factor can shrink the list further, and the rule reads the list at request, confirm and finish.
The doors checked for (1e), app/api/auth/**: password/login needs the password; password/first-login opens only an account still on its one-time password, and an invite renews a one-time password only `.eq("must_change_password", true)` (lib/access-invite.ts:99), never one the owner chose; password/forgot and reset-code are the inbox reset this rule covers; password/register makes new accounts only; oauth start, callback and complete never join an existing account by email (lib/auth/oauth.ts:17, email_in_use at :511); stepup/email mails a code to an email factor and mints a step-up token, no session; session is a wallet signature; attach-wallet, nonce, wallet/jwt, jwks, identities, mfa/** and passkey/** open no session. Every session is minted in six places (`grep -rn "mintUserSession\|completePasswordReset"`): the OAuth callback, register, reset-code, recovery/complete, password-login and lib/hunter/publish.ts (the hunter account, server side). No emailed login code exists: `grep -rniE "magic.?link|login code|sign-in code"` over app and lib has no hit outside comments on "email login".
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) A guardian recovery (app/api/recovery/complete) is one guardian's inbox opening a session when the threshold is 1: a third person's inbox, not the account's. The code that starts the mail path goes to the account's own confirmed address, so that session cannot start it without that inbox too, and the reset now tells every address. Not changed. (b) An OAuth login rewrites its identity's email from the provider (lib/auth/oauth.ts:476): whoever controls a Google account with a non-Gmail address can change it. That swaps one address for another; the count stays, and the code still goes to the confirmed login or users address. (c) In this commit the disconnect still asks no factor (DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 1); confirm and finish then refuse, so a disconnect can stop the path, not finish it. The next commit gates it.
Evidence: INFERRED from reading at this commit: the grep outputs quoted above, run 2026-11-05. VERIFIED through the real routes: a list that shrank after the code went out refuses at confirm, and at finish (lib/__tests__/inbox-door.test.ts). REPORTED from DEC-2026-11-05-49: `factors all 200 */0`, so no live account has a factor today. Blind spots: the grep reads table names in app and lib only; the app calls 33 named RPCs (`grep -rhno ".rpc(..."`), none named for these tables, and their SQL bodies were not read; a write path added later is not covered.
Revert: revert this commit.

### DEC-2026-11-05-53: Disconnecting Google or X takes every factor and tells every address, the leaving one included; closes DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 1
Context: DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 1: DELETE /api/auth/identities/[provider] read no factor and sent no mail, so a stolen session could drop an address from the recovery mails unheard, and on a wallet account with Google leave the account with no address at all. Kev, 2026-11-05: "fix the offene sachen".
Options: requireAddFactor, as DEC-2026-11-05-40 suggested (rejected: without a factor it asks for a session under ten minutes old, and the decided design says "without a factor: as today, plus the mail"); requireStepUp, one factor (rejected: a disconnect takes a way in and an address, as a factor's removal takes a factor); requireAllFactors, not mandatory (chosen).
Decision: the route answers "not connected" (404) and the last way in (409) first, so a refusal asks and spends no factor; then requireAllFactors with a new scope, disconnect:google or disconnect:x (lib/webauthn.ts SCOPE); then everyAddress before the delete, so a failed read removes nothing; once the delete stands, mailEach to those addresses: "Google was disconnected from your Enki account (time). It can no longer be used to sign in to it. If that was you, there is nothing to do." and, if not, RESET_ADVICE. A disconnect the race recount puts back mails nobody. Settings' Disconnect goes through guarded with that scope, the client path a factor's removal uses (withStepUp asks each missing factor in turn); a cancel at a factor shows no toast, as Connect does. The step-up dialog says "Changing your security settings takes every factor you set up" for it.
Mine, for Kev to challenge: (1) The scope names the provider, so a token for one cannot disconnect the other. (2) The mail goes to every address past the limiter, as the recovery mails do, not through mailSecurityNotice's one address. (3) The branch where the account was deleted during the race answers removed with no mail: the account is gone.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) Without a factor a stolen session still disconnects, as before; now every address hears, the leaving one once and then never again. (b) A disconnect does not end the sessions that came in through that login; no sign-out control exists (Kev, DEC-2026-11-05-41 (a)). (c) The dialog has no sentence of its own for a disconnect.

The wallet JWT refuses a password account whose login email is unconfirmed (app/api/auth/wallet/jwt/route.ts:87-91), email_verified_at was written only by a first login (app/api/auth/password/first-login/route.ts:68) and a reset through the inbox (lib/password-reset.ts:37), and the register route writes none (app/api/auth/password/register/route.ts:89). Live, read-only (OpenAPI and HEAD counts, 2026-11-07): password_credentials `200 0-2/3`, unconfirmed and not on a one-time password `200 0-1/2`, must_change_password true `200 */0`.
Options: (a) a new table in SQL 75, the routes answering 503 until it runs (rejected: Kev runs every SQL at the very end, so the window would say "not available" until then, and an existing table fits); (b) email_verification_tokens, live, empty and read by no code (`id:uuid(pk), user_id:uuid(fk), email_lookup_hash:text, token_hash:text, purpose:text, expires_at, used_at, created_at`, `200 */0`) (rejected: no migration in the repo declares it, `grep -rl email_verification_tokens` over migrations, sql-to-run and docs found nothing, so a CHECK on purpose and what email_lookup_hash must hold cannot be learned without a write); (c) password_reset_tokens, where the forgot route keeps its codes (`token, user_id, expires_at, created_at`, token the primary key; chosen).
Decision: GET /api/auth/password/confirm-email answers { needed, email }: needed only for a signed-in password account with email_verified_at null and must_change_password false, email masked as the guardian page masks ("ow…@example.test"), null otherwise. POST mails a 7 digit code to password_credentials.email of that account, never to an address in the body; only its SHA-256 is stored, one live code per account, 15 min. POST ./verify { code } spends every code of the account, then sets email_verified_at = now where it is null, and nothing else. Already confirmed: { confirmed: true }, nothing sent. No password: 404. Still on an invitation's one-time password: 409, whose first login confirms. Limits: request 10 per network in 10 min (the forgot route's) and 3 per account in 15 min; verify 20 per network in 15 min and the reset-code route's own 5 per address in 15 min (the same key, rateLimitKey(req, "auth:resetcode", email)). Wrong code, expired code and no code waiting each have their own words. Ban tolerant, as the wallet JWT route is; a deleted account has no session left (softDelete evicts them, app/api/account/delete/route.ts:30-48), so it gets 401 as on every session route. Shared code: lib/confirm-email.ts.
Consequences of (c), inside the decision: (1) A confirm code is a valid reset code for the same login email within its 15 minutes, and a reset code from the forgot route confirms the email: both are mailed to that one inbox and prove it, and whoever reads it can reset anyway. (2) A forgot request replaces a live confirm code and the reverse; the latest mail's code is the one that works. (3) Both doors spend the same five tries per address, so the code's guessing budget stays where reset-code set it. (4) Two accounts' codes colliding on the token primary key fail the insert: the request answers 503 and the owner asks again (the forgot route ignores that error; unchanged).
Mine, for Kev to challenge: (1) Wrong, expired and none waiting are told apart, where reset-code says "Wrong or expired code" to anyone: here the session already names the account, so the words reveal nothing new. (2) With no mail set up, a server outside production logs the code, as the forgot route does (app/api/auth/password/forgot/route.ts:59-61), and the request answers 502. (3) The confirm mail tells someone who did not ask to reset the password, as RESET_ADVICE does (lib/mfa.ts:68): a request needs a signed-in session, so a mail nobody asked for means someone else holds one.
Evidence: VERIFIED lib/__tests__/confirm-email.test.ts through the real routes, the real session lookup and the real forgot, reset-code and wallet JWT routes, another account's unconfirmed login email, live code, session and ban first in every table and unchanged after each test: `Tests  25 passed (25)`. In-memory mutants, baseline `Tests  25 passed (25)`, fsModuleCache off: `killed 30 / 31`. The survivor is equivalent: verify also writing must_change_password false (`SURVIVED verify-sets-more: Tests  25 passed (25)`) writes false over false, as an account with true is refused before the update; writing updated_at or pw_hash there is killed. Live schema read-only with scratchpad confirm-email/schema.mjs and evt.mjs (no row values printed). The whole suite count is in the commit message. Blind spots: a fake PostgREST; no mail was sent; the limits live in each server process's memory (lib/rate-limit.ts:8), as every other auth route's.
Revert: revert this commit.

### DEC-2026-11-07-04: A new confirm code is stored before the older ones go, and they go only once its mail is out (correction to DEC-2026-11-07-01)
Context: Review of a97be9f1..99b60c19. DEC-2026-11-07-01 said the request keeps "one live code per account" and, consequence (2), "the latest mail's code is the one that works". Both were false: the route deleted the account's codes, then inserted the new one, then mailed it. Racing requests all deleted before any of them inserted, so every code stayed live, VERIFIED by the reviewer's probe, re-run at 99b60c19: `PROBE A1 mails 2 live codes 2`, `PROBE A3 mailed 3 still live 3`. A resend whose mail failed had already deleted the code in the inbox, VERIFIED: `S1 second request: {"status":502,"body":{"error":"The code could not be sent. Try again in a minute."}}` then `S1 the code from the first mail: {"status":400,"body":{"error":"Wrong code. Check the email and try again."}}`. Why the tests missed it: they made one request at a time, and their one failed mail had no code before it.
Options: (a) delete, insert, mail, as before (rejected: both defects); (b) insert, delete the others, mail (rejected: a failed mail still leaves only a code nobody got); (c) insert, mail, then delete the others, and a failed mail deletes only the new code (chosen, the reviewer's fix).
Decision: app/api/auth/password/confirm-email/route.ts stores the new code, mails it, and only then deletes the account's other codes (`.eq("user_id", userId).neq("token", token)`). A mail that fails or a mailer that throws: the new code is deleted (`.eq("token", token).eq("user_id", userId)`), 502, and the code already in the inbox keeps working; should that delete fail too, the code nobody got expires in its 15 minutes. A failed clear after the mail went out: 503, never "sent"; the mailed code stays stored and works, the older ones expire in their 15 minutes. Racing confirm requests: each removes every code but its own once its mail is out, so at most one is left, and none when they cross (fails closed: each of those mails then answers "Wrong code", and one new request works). The forgot route keeps its own delete-then-insert (out of this window's scope, returned to Kev), so a forgot request racing a confirm request can still leave two codes: INFERRED from its order (app/api/auth/password/forgot/route.ts:45-50); in the reviewer's interleaving it left one (`PROBE A2 mails 2 live codes 1`).
Evidence: VERIFIED lib/__tests__/confirm-email.test.ts `Tests  30 passed (30)`, five new tests: a failed and a throwing mail leave the inbox code working and keep none nobody got; three racing requests leave at most one live code, and only a mailed one; a failed insert mails nothing; a failed clear after the mail is a 503 and the mailed code works; in production a failed mail logs no code. In-memory mutants, baseline `Tests  30 passed (30)`, fsModuleCache off: `killed 10 / 10` (the old order back; no clear; the clear taking the new code too; a failed mail keeping the new code, or dropping every code; the clear before the mail; the insert failure and the clear failure ignored; the mailer's throw uncaught; the code logged in production). The reviewers' probes re-run on this tree: `PROBE A1 mails 2 live codes 0`, `PROBE A3 mailed 3 still live 0` (`Tests  3 passed | 7 skipped (10)`); `S1 the code from the first mail: {"status":200,"body":{"confirmed":true}}` (`Tests  1 passed | 2 skipped (3)`). Equivalent mutant, not run: the failed mail's delete without `.eq("user_id", userId)` (the token is the primary key). The whole suite count is in the commit message. Blind spot: a fake PostgREST, which interleaves at each await; on real PostgREST each delete is one statement over committed rows, so the same bound holds (INFERRED).
Revert: revert this commit.

Context: Review of a97be9f1..99b60c19. ### DEC-2026-11-07-10: No code left: one code to every address, all entered, removes the lost factor at once; fewer than two addresses and the path is not offered
Context: Kev, 2026-11-07: "nein, keine 5 tage scheiß wartezeit! wenn jemand zugriff hat auf all seine geräte uind resetten kann, so soll das auch resetted werden", "warn mails an alle". NIST SP 800-63B-4 "Recovery at AAL2", read live 2026-11-07 (REPORTED by the brief): "Two recovery codes obtained using different methods". This entry is (c), added beside the 5 day path and switched to in Settings; the waiting machinery goes in its own deletion commit, after the guardians path.
Options: one code to the first confirmed address, as before, with no wait (rejected: one inbox would remove a factor, the hole DEC-2026-11-05-49 point 1 named); new tables for the codes (rejected: SQL 74 has not run, so its mfa_recovery row takes one more column); one code mailed to every address, any one entered (rejected: one inbox again); a code to each address, every one entered in one form (chosen, the brief).
Decision: POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery/mail { factor } sends one 6 digit code to each address of everyAddress (lib/security-notice.ts), stored only as keyed HMACs over user_id:address:code in mfa_recovery.code_hashes (text[], new in SQL 74), for 10 minutes (lib/mfa.ts CODE_TTL_MS), one live set per account (a new send replaces the last), one send a minute and five a day across every send (lib/mfa.ts sendRefusal), conditional on the row as read so two sends at once send one set. The answer names the addresses masked (lib/confirm-email.ts maskEmail) in the order the codes go back. POST ./confirm { codes } checks every code against its own address before anything moves: the attempt is claimed first on the counter recovery codes use (5 tries, the lock ladder), the set is spent with a conditional update, then the account's unused recovery codes go, then the factor (all passkeys as one), and every address hears ("A code sent to each of your email addresses removed ... The recovery codes you had left stopped working too: ..."). A failure after the spend brings the set back. A new factor of the named kind closes the set (codesForNewFactor, as before). Fewer than two addresses: 409 TOO_FEW, nothing written, nothing mailed; Settings shows mailRefused in place of No code left, now from the address count instead of the door rule, naming a recovery code and the step to a second address.
Mine, for Kev to challenge: (1) The address of an email factor named as lost gets no code and does not count toward the two: whoever reads that inbox holds the factor, and an owner who lost it could never enter its code; a planted email factor could otherwise block its own removal by the owner (the case DEC-2026-11-05-46 weighed). It still gets the removal mail. (2) The codes are bound to their address, and the list is sorted (by code unit, ignoring case) so the send and the confirm agree on the order; a list whose length changed since the send answers 409 "Your email addresses changed since the codes went out. Ask for new ones." and spends no try; one whose address was swapped at the same length fails as a wrong code. (3) The addresses are read before the try is claimed, as everywhere in this file: a failed read answers 500 and spends nothing. (4) A set where any one mail did not go out answers 502: it can never be entered, and the next send (after a minute) replaces it. (5) The old one-door rule (DEC-2026-11-05-50/51) is subsumed: two addresses or more each confirm, so no single inbox, door or not, removes a factor. It stays only on the old 5 day routes until the deletion commit removes them with addressList and ONE_DOOR. Changed with it: one address that signs in by nothing (a wallet account with only an email factor's address) used to be enough for the 5 day path and is now too few. (6) The disconnect mail (DEC-2026-11-06-02) now adds its sentence when fewer than two addresses are left with a factor, door or not: "This account now has fewer than two email addresses, so until it has a second, a lost factor can be removed only with a recovery code." (7) The Settings sentence "Did not add the code by email yourself? Remove that first: its address gets the link that cancels any other removal." is gone with the switch: no path Settings starts mails a cancel link any more. (8) Transitional, until the deletion commit: a send overwrites a 5 day wait on the same row without a cancel mail. No such row can exist anywhere, as SQL 74 has not run (VERIFIED live: `mfa_recovery: 404`).
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) Accepted by Kev with the rule: someone holding the session AND every inbox of the account removes a factor at once; every address hears. (b) An account with one address and no code left has no mail path: a recovery code or guardians (next commit) only, and Settings says so while the factor is still there. (c) A send costs every address a mail; five sets a day per account bound it.

### DEC-2026-11-07-11: Guardians remove a lost factor at once: two confirmed guardians or more, the owner's threshold never below two, every address hears
Context: Kev, 2026-11-07: "ok go for the guardians", "nein, es soll sofort aufgemacht werden sofern die guardians das bestätigen! keine wartezeit, wir locken niemanden der verifiziert wurde.", "warn mails an alle". The decided rule's (b): a signed-in owner, 2 confirmed guardians say yes, instant. The brief: reuse the guardian request and approval tables and routes where they fit; they serve the guardian password reset today; keep that working.
Found, against the brief (VERIFIED live 2026-11-07, read-only, OpenAPI, scratchpad recovery-package/schema.mjs and defaults.mjs): recovery_requests holds the columns of an older design that are NOT NULL with no default: `recovery_requests contact_email_ct default: null`, the same for contact_email_iv, contact_email_tag, contact_email_kid, contact_email_lookup_hash and `layer default: null`; `recovery_requests rows: 200 */0`. app/api/recovery/request/route.ts:58-67 inserts only user_id, status, owner_key_hash and expires_at, so the guardian password reset cannot start live today and never has (INFERRED from the schema and the 0 rows; no write was made to prove it). Confirmed guardians live: `guardians email confirmed: 200 */0` and `*/0` for every other type, `recovery_guardians rows: 200 0-0/1`.
Options: new tables in SQL 74 for the asks (rejected: the brief says reuse, and the existing pair has what an ask needs: a request per account with a status and an expiry, an approval per guardian); fill the six old columns with placeholders (rejected: junk in a table that holds encrypted contact data by design); SQL 74 drops their NOT NULL, as migrations/2026-07-12-recovery-guardians.sql did for recovery_guardians' old columns (chosen: it also lets the password reset's insert land once it ran).
Decision: SQL 74 adds recovery_requests.factor (CHECK passkey, totp, email; NULL is a password reset's request), drops NOT NULL on the six columns, and adds a unique partial index, one pending ask per account. POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery/guardians { factor }: needs the factor enrolled and two confirmed guardians or more by email or wallet; the number that must say yes is max(2, min(lib/recovery/threshold.ts recoveryThreshold, guardians asked)). One request for 7 days, one recovery_approvals row per guardian with only the SHA-256 of a 48 hex token. Each email guardian gets "@<handle> asks for your help getting back into Enki Art": who asks, "Your yes helps remove @<handle>'s lost security factor so they can get into their money again. The moment N guardians say yes, it is removed.", "Only say yes if @<handle> asked you themselves, by phone or in person, not only by a message: someone who took over their account can write to you in their name.", the link /guardian?factor=<id>&g=<guardian>&t=<token>, and "If they did not ask you themselves, do nothing: without your yes nothing changes, and the request ends in 7 days." A wallet guardian's link (no token) comes back to the owner to send; on /guardian that wallet signs lib/guardian-message.ts guardianFactorMessage(requestId), checked with ed25519 against the guardian's stored address, as the invite's signature is. Every address of the owner hears at once, the guardians named masked. The yes that reaches the number claims the request (pending to completed, conditional), deletes the owner's unused recovery codes, removes the factor (all passkeys as one) and mails every address ("Your guardians removed ... N of them said yes. ... If it was not, someone talked your guardians round and is using your session: ..."). A failure after the claim puts the request back to pending, and the guardian's next yes finishes it. DELETE withdraws (session only, it can only make the account safer). A no or silence changes nothing: there is no "no" button, only "do nothing". A new factor of the named kind cancels the ask (codesForNewFactor), as it closes a mailed code set. GET /api/auth/mfa/recovery carries guardians { askable, needed, ask: { factor, approved, needed, expiresAt, wallets } | null }; Settings, Lost a factor, shows "Ask my guardians" with two or more, "Asking your guardians needs two confirmed guardians or more, by email or wallet. Add them under Guardians." with fewer, and a running ask's count, its end date, a "Copy the link for <wallet>" per wallet guardian, and Withdraw. The guardian's yes goes through app/api/recovery/approve (already public in proxy.ts): GET ?factor=&g= for the page, POST with token or signature.
Mine, for Kev to challenge: (1) Only email and wallet guardians count and are asked. An authenticator guardian is the owner's own app (migrations/2026-07-12-recovery-guardians.sql: "'authenticator' = your own TOTP") and a phone guardian has no ask built (the password reset path asks email guardians only, app/api/recovery/request/route.ts:48); counting either would let fewer than two other people say yes. (2) The number is capped at the guardians that can be asked, or an owner whose threshold counts an authenticator guardian could never reach it. (3) The email guardian's proof is a 192 bit token in the link, not the 7 digit code the password reset mails: a session holder knows the request and guardian ids (Settings and the ask's answer show them), and a 7 digit code behind a per-instance, per-network limiter can be guessed across networks within 7 days. (4) A factor ask has no owner key, and the old code path now refuses a request without one (one condition in app/api/recovery/approve/route.ts): before it, a guardian whose yes was already counted on a factor ask could post any 7 digits there, skip the code check (the route skips it for an approved row) and flip the ask to 'approved'. No password reset request lacks a key: the request route always writes one. (5) The start mail to every address names the guardians asked, so a guardian planted earlier shows (see DEC-2026-11-07-12). (6) Five asks a day per account, refused asks included, per instance (lib/rate-limit.ts): every ask mails the guardians. (7) A guardian removed since their yes no longer counts; a factor already gone at the number closes the ask as cancelled and mails nothing. (8) The wallet buttons on the guardian's page reuse EnkiCardButton rather than the invite view's own button markup; no refactor of the invite view in this commit. (9) The module hashes the guardians' tokens with its own one-line SHA-256: importing lib/password-reset's sha256 loaded lib/password-auth, which hashes with AUTH_PEPPER when it loads, and the whole suite went red on the files that import lib/mfa-recovery without that setting (`FAIL  lib/__tests__/attach-wallet-ownership.test.ts`, `FAIL  lib/__tests__/ban-funds-door.test.ts`, `Error: AUTH_PEPPER not configured ... lib/password-reset.ts:8:1`, `Test Files  2 failed | 573 passed | 1 skipped (576)`); a neighbour run had not shown it.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) Accepted by Kev with the rule: a Gmail thief holding the session who talks two guardians round gets in at once; every address hears at the ask and at the removal. (b) An owner with fewer than two email or wallet guardians, no code and one address has no way back; Settings says so while the factor is still there (mailRefusal: "No recovery code is left either, and fewer than two guardians can be asked, so a lost factor cannot be removed now."). (c) The ask's limit and the approve route's limiter live in each server process's memory, as every other auth limiter. (d) A guardian's link is a bearer token for 7 days: whoever reads that guardian's mail can say yes as them; the warning sentence is the defence, and it takes the number of guardians. (e) After SQL 74 runs, the guardian password reset can start for the first time; it is unchanged otherwise, and its own threshold can be 1 (DEC-2026-11-05-52 residual a).

### DEC-2026-11-07-12: With a factor, a re-invite of a guardian takes every factor; what else makes or confirms a guardian, as found
Context: The brief's (2b): guardians now remove a lost factor at once (DEC-2026-11-07-11), so a guardian a stolen session plants would strip the owner's factors. Verify whether inviting or confirming a guardian on an account with a factor asks for every factor today; if not, gate it like a factor's removal (requireAllFactors, the client's guarded step-up).
Found, read at 3823d79d (app/api/recovery/guardians/route.ts): (a) adding a guardian, POST with guardianType, passes requireAddFactor(req, userId, "guardians") (:273), which with a factor is requireAllFactors (lib/webauthn.ts:209): every factor, VERIFIED below with two factors and one token. (b) PATCH threshold: the same gate (:393), VERIFIED the same way. (c) DELETE a guardian: requireStepUp, one factor (:420); it removes, it plants nothing. (d) Not gated: the re-invite branch (reinviteId, :252) resets a pending or unresponsive guardian to pending with a new invite token and mails it, session only. A guardian planted before the owner's first factor and gone unresponsive could be invited again by a session that holds no factor, and accept: VERIFIED, the gate removed in memory answers 200 with no token (`killed   reinvite-ungated` below is the code as it was). (e) Not gated, on purpose: confirming an authenticator or phone guardian (verifyId, phoneVerifyId, phoneResendId, before the gate). lib/__tests__/mfa-enroll.test.ts "still let an added authenticator guardian be confirmed without one" pins it, those rows were added through the gate, and neither type is ever asked to approve anything: the password reset asks email guardians only (app/api/recovery/request/route.ts:48), the factor path email and wallet ones (DEC-2026-11-07-11 point 1). (f) The guardian's own accept on /guardian (app/api/recovery/guardians/confirm/route.ts) is the invitee's act: no owner is there to ask.
Options: gate every owner branch before the add gate (rejected: an authenticator or phone guardian added with every factor would then ask every factor a second time to be confirmed, for a guardian no path asks); gate the re-invite only (chosen).
Decision: the re-invite branch asks requireAllFactors(req, userId, "guardians") first; with no factor it goes as before. Settings' re-invite goes through guarded("guardians", ...), the path every other guardian change takes.
Residual risk, inside the decision: (a) An invite sent while the account had no factor can still be accepted after the first factor is added, by whoever holds that link: the accept is the invitee's, and nothing records whether a factor existed at the invite. The start mail of a guardian ask names every guardian asked (DEC-2026-11-07-11 point 5), and Settings lists them; a stolen session on a factor-free account can plant a factor too, the case DEC-2026-11-05-45 and -55 bound. (b) Removing a guardian keeps one factor (c): a session with one factor of two can take guardians away, not add them.

### DEC-2026-11-07-15: Every security notice goes to every address of the account, the one just connected included; closes DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 2
Context: DEC-2026-11-05-40 point 2: mailSecurityNotice sent each notice to one ranked address (lib/security-notice.ts securityNoticeAddress), so a stolen session under ten minutes old that connected its own Google outranked the owner's unconfirmed login email, and the factor, wallet, export and withdrawal notices went to the attacker only. Options: also send to the unconfirmed login email when the ranked address is an identity or a factor (DEC-2026-11-05-40's smallest fix; rejected: the brief says every address); every address (chosen).

### DEC-2026-11-07-17: A forgot request stores its code before the older ones go, and they go only once its mail is out (the order of DEC-2026-11-07-04)
Context: The review of DEC-2026-11-07-01, returned to Kev in DEC-2026-11-07-04: app/api/auth/password/forgot/route.ts deleted the account's codes, then inserted the new one, then mailed it. Racing requests all deleted before any inserted, so several reset codes stayed live (REPORTED by the review; VERIFIED here: the old order put back in memory turns the new race test red, `killed   old-order-back: Tests  4 failed | 3 passed (7)`), and a forgot request racing a confirm request could leave two (INFERRED in DEC-2026-11-07-04 from the order; the reviewer's interleaving left one, `PROBE A2 mails 2 live codes 1`). A resend whose mail failed had already deleted the code in the inbox. The brief: use the insert-first, then delete-the-others order.
Options: the old order (rejected: the defect); insert, delete the others, mail (rejected: a failed mail leaves only a code nobody got); insert, mail, then delete the others, and a failed mail deletes only the new code (chosen, as the confirm route does since DEC-2026-11-07-04).
Decision: the route stores the new code, mails it, and only then deletes the account's other codes (`.eq("user_id", ...).neq("token", token)`). A mail that does not go out, or a mailer that throws, deletes only the new code, and the code already in the inbox keeps working. A code that cannot be stored is not mailed. The answer stays { ok: true } in every case, as before, so nothing on screen tells one address from another.

In production no code is logged (tested). The confirm route deletes its own new code when no mail went out, also outside production, so the code it logs there no longer works; not changed here (outside this item). (2) A failed clear after the mail went out is logged and still answers ok: the older codes then expire in their 15 minutes, as DEC-2026-11-07-04 accepted for the confirm route's 503. Here a 503 would tell an address with an account from one without.

(b) The codes are bounded per account, not per request: several mails can still be in an inbox, only the newest works.

Esc is heard on the document as it bubbles, leaves an Esc already used, and stops it: the step-up dialog (Radix) hears first on the document's capture and marks it used, VERIFIED node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dismissable-layer/dist/index.mjs:63-65 `if (!event.defaultPrevented && onDismiss) { event.preventDefault(); onDismiss(); }`, so one Esc closes that dialog alone, and the next closes the sheet before the panel hears it; lib/__tests__/esc-top-layer.test.ts lists the sheet with the layers that stay open under others. Tab stays inside (the kit's trapStep, as BottomSheet), the focus starts on [data-autofocus], else the first control, else the sheet, on each step, and goes back to the opener if it is still on the page; lockScroll holds the page; a press that begins in the card and ends on the veil does not close it (StudioDialog's rule). ### DEC-2026-11-08-46: The wallet picker's card is above its veil again (Tailwind could not read a glued class)
Context: Kev, 2026-11-08, with a screenshot of the whole wallet picker blurred: "warum ist der walletlogin zerschossen?". VERIFIED on 3008 (landing, Log in, Continue with Wallet): the dialog's computed z-index was `auto` while its veil had 2000, and no stylesheet held a rule for `z-[2001]` (the veil's `.z-\[2000\] { z-index: 2000; }` was there). Cause: 91eb9865 (my restyle, DEC-2026-11-07-37) turned the class into the template literal `...overflow-hidden z-[2001]${inApp ? " wp-app" : ""}`; Tailwind's scanner does not extract a class glued to `${`, so it wrote no rule and the veil covered the card.
Options: a space before the expression (rejected: the landing picker's markup gains a trailing space, and window-type.test.ts holds it byte-equal); cn() (larger); two plain strings by inApp (chosen: the landing markup stays byte-equal).
Decision: `className={inApp ? "... z-[2001] wp-app" : "... z-[2001]"}`; old-card-tokens.test.ts:350, which held the glued string, now holds this one. lib/__tests__/tailwind-glue.test.ts fails on any tracked .tsx with an arbitrary-value class glued to `${` (one existed: this one) and pins the picker's string.
Evidence: VERIFIED `git show HEAD:components/WalletPickerModal.tsx | grep -c ']${'` = 1 before, the new test green after; the browser check after the fix is in the report. Committed together with DEC-45 to keep the gate runs few (Kev: credits are low).
Revert: revert this commit.
